     1	# Add Dispatch Sandbox Enforcement
     2	
     3	> Parent roadmap: `dispatch-governance` (`dg-07`)
     4	> Change ID: `add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement`
     5	> Prerequisites: dg-02, dg-03, dg-05, and dg-06 are landed
     6	
     7	## Why
     8	
     9	The router now chooses an isolation posture and the orchestrator carries that immutable
    10	decision to execution, but local vendor CLI processes still run with the host user's OS
    11	authority. A `worktree` prevents concurrent agents from sharing one checkout; it does not
    12	prevent reads of sibling/user-home data, writes elsewhere, or arbitrary egress. The coordinator's
    13	network policy is likewise advisory because it is checked only by callers that volunteer a
    14	domain.
    15	
    16	dg-07 closes the local execution gap. A shared local-process backend consumes the exact dg-06
    17	decision, renders the coordinator's policy for Anthropic Sandbox Runtime (SRT), and applies the
    18	result to every vendor CLI lifecycle command: synchronous invocation, asynchronous submission,
    19	polling, and the autopilot local-provider harness.
    20	
    21	## What Changes
    22	
    23	### Immutable execution context
    24	
    25	Dispatch receives a versioned execution context containing the complete dg-06 enforcement
    26	projection, canonical digest of the persisted routing context, one authoritative isolation,
    27	canonical worktree root, and provenance.
    28	The enforcement layer never re-runs routing. Standalone review-panel calls that have no routed
    29	context resolve the already-landed dg-05 fallback once from the exact `agents.yaml` lane.
    30	Routed callers carry the complete context in phase payload v2; every adapter lifecycle method
    31	accepts that context explicitly instead of reconstructing it from cwd.
    32	
    33	### Coordinator-owned network-policy export and audit
    34	
    35	`NetworkPolicyService` gains an exact-agent export. It returns the active profile-specific and
    36	global rules, a closed default-deny contract, schema revision, and a deterministic digest.
    37	Rendering is conservative: SRT denies take precedence, so conflicting authored rules may become
    38	narrower but never wider. A malformed or unavailable cold-start export fails closed before vendor
    39	launch; only a successfully exported empty allow set is a valid deny-all policy.
    40	
    41	A narrow sandbox-execution audit endpoint durably and idempotently records applied and degraded
    42	outcomes. If the coordinator is unavailable, a locked mode-0600 JSONL outbox under the operator's
    43	XDG state directory is fsynced and retried oldest-first on later calls. An unsandboxed fallback is
    44	allowed only after either the coordinator event or the durable outbox record succeeds.
    45	
    46	### Pure renderer and lifecycle-owning backend
    47	
    48	`skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py` provides:
    49	
    50	- pure, deterministic SRT settings rendering;
    51	- mode-aware filesystem policy (`review` has no project write roots; write-capable modes are
    52	  confined to the canonical worktree root; user-home reads are denied with narrow worktree/tool
    53	  carve-outs; every lane gets an ephemeral vendor-state root);
    54	- a prepared-command lifecycle that owns a unique mode-0600 settings file, sanitized environment,
    55	  runtime identity, policy digest, process group, and cleanup;
    56	- an additive renderer seam for future runtimes.
    57	
    58	The reviewed runtime is `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` 0.0.77 on Node >=20.11.0. The repository
    59	pins the package and integrity and never installs it during dispatch. Setup/CI install the pin;
    60	runtime discovery is explicit absolute override, then the primary checkout resolved through the
    61	linked worktree's common Git directory, then unavailable. The runtime is accepted only when
    62	package metadata and integrity match. On Linux
    63	the preflight also verifies `bubblewrap`, `socat`,
    64	`ripgrep`, user-namespace capability, architecture/seccomp support, and a real no-op SRT launch.
    65	
    66	Official runtime sources:
    67	
    68	- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime
    69	- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/blob/main/README.md
    70	- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/blob/main/package.json
    71	- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-9gqj-5w7c-vx47
    72	
    73	### One local command backend
    74	
    75	The shared backend replaces direct vendor subprocess launches in `CliVendorAdapter` sync submit,
    76	async submit and poll paths, and in `autopilot/scripts/provider_dispatch.py`. Poll enforcement
    77	failures are collection failures retried to the existing deadline, not terminal remote-task
    78	failures. A structural guard
    79	prevents future vendor CLI subprocess sinks outside the backend. Non-sandbox decisions preserve
    80	argv, stdin, cwd, timeout, and result behavior.
    81	
    82	### Loud, bounded degradation
    83	
    84	Fail-open is restricted to facts known before a vendor process starts: unsupported OS, missing or
    85	incompatible pinned runtime, or failed platform capability preflight. Those cases warn, durably
    86	audit `applied=false`, and run the original command. Unsafe roots, malformed policy, settings
    87	materialization errors, and audit/outbox failures fail closed. Once SRT starts, a timeout or
    88	unknown failure never triggers an unsandboxed retry because doing so could execute work twice.
    89	
    90	## Scope Boundary
    91	
    92	This change protects against accidental or confused local CLI behavior after sandbox startup.
    93	It does not claim containment of a malicious vendor executable, a compromised runtime, same-user
    94	races, damage inside an authorized writable root, or exfiltration through an allowed destination
    95	such as GitHub. It strips proxy and code-injection environment variables required to preserve the
    96	SRT boundary. dg-07 sandbox lanes require environment-backed authentication; file-backed login
    97	state remains ineligible. Credentials deliberately supplied to a CLI remain readable by that CLI.
    98	Request-time secret substitution is dg-08; broader credential brokering and cloud execution remain
    99	owned by `add-sandboxed-harness-execution`.
   100	
   101	dg-03's factual `posture.filesystem` means a per-session workspace exists; it is not a security
   102	attestation and never satisfies a router request for `sandbox`. Wrapping a local submission CLI
   103	also does not imply that a remote worker is sandboxed.
   104	
   105	## Approaches Considered
   106	
   107	### Shared SRT local-process backend (selected)
   108	
   109	One policy renderer and one lifecycle-owning runner cover every current local CLI sink. It enforces
   110	the already-authored isolation and network decisions without creating a second router.
   111	
   112	### Vendor-native flags only
   113	
   114	Rejected. Vendor flags differ, omit network enforcement, and leave vendors without a native
   115	sandbox unprotected.
   116	
   117	### Coordinator-managed containers
   118	
   119	Deferred. A container/control-plane backend belongs to the downstream sandboxed-harness change;
   120	dg-07 supplies the local backend and renderer seam it consumes.
   121	
   122	## Impact
   123	
   124	- New shared runtime: `skills/shared/sandbox_profile.py` and local process backend helpers.
   125	- Modified execution sinks: review dispatcher and autopilot local-provider dispatch.
   126	- Modified coordinator: exact-agent policy export and durable sandbox audit endpoint.
   127	- Modified config projection: effective per-mode isolation reaches standalone adapters.
   128	- New pinned optional tool dependency: SRT 0.0.77.
   129	- New contracts, tests, operational documentation, and real-runtime probes.
   130	- New PR-triggered Ubuntu/macOS GitHub Actions evidence gate, with linked-worktree and configured-
   131	  vendor CLI passes bound to the tested SHA.
   132	
   133	## Rollback
   134	
   135	Removing a mode's `sandbox` decision restores the byte-compatible local process path. Removing or
   136	breaking the runtime does not silently claim enforcement: the preflight records a durable degraded
   137	event before the legacy command may run.
     1	# Design: Dispatch sandbox enforcement
     2	
     3	## Context
     4	
     5	dg-02 supplies structured vendor results, dg-03 supplies factual environment posture, dg-05
     6	pins isolation vocabulary and fallback, and dg-06 carries one immutable routing decision. dg-07
     7	is the execution consumer. The current two subprocess call families are the multi-vendor review
     8	dispatcher and autopilot's local Pi provider.
     9	
    10	## Decisions
    11	
    12	### D1 — Consume one immutable execution context
    13	
    14	`DispatchExecutionContext` is a normative enforcement projection of dg-06: decision id, item id,
    15	phase, attempt, dispatch work id, every assignment field, and a canonical digest of the full
    16	persisted routing context, plus enforcement scope and canonical root. The roadmap host constructs
    17	it at the dispatch boundary and passes it through `PhaseDispatchPayload.execution_context`.
    18	Payload v2 removes the legacy top-level isolation authority; a compatibility reader rejects any
    19	legacy isolation value that disagrees with the embedded context. `CliVendorAdapter.dispatch()`,
    20	`dispatch_async()`, and `poll_for_result()` receive the same explicit context. Standalone panel
    21	callers construct one context at their adapter boundary from the exact lane's mode override, then
    22	entry value. A router-sourced context requires router correlation and the assignment digest. No
    23	renderer or backend calls routing or derives a sandbox root from ambient process cwd. Root safety
    24	checks apply only while preparing `sandbox`; `none` and `worktree` preserve legacy cwd behavior.
    25	
    26	Context producers are explicit:
    27	
    28	| Caller | Assignment fields | Execution root |
    29	| --- | --- | --- |
    30	| Routed roadmap/autopilot phase | Copy the dg-06 enforcement projection and digest into payload v2; it overrides the old phase-level `worktree` default | Host adds the validated managed-worktree root |
    31	| Standalone vendor panel | Resolve exact-lane mode override, then entry isolation, exactly once | Adapter validates its explicit invocation cwd |
    32	| Autopilot local provider | Consume payload v2 unchanged; no legacy reconstruction | Required in the embedded context |
    33	
    34	dg-03 posture is diagnostic evidence only. Its filesystem bit means a per-session workspace, not
    35	credential containment; its network bit does not prove equivalence to the active coordinator
    36	policy. Neither bit satisfies `isolation=sandbox`.
    37	
    38	### D2 — One local process backend, not one list wrapper
    39	
    40	All vendor CLI execution sites call `skills/shared/local_process_backend.py`. The pure renderer in
    41	`sandbox_profile.py` returns settings and a digest; an impure prepared-command context manager
    42	validates runtime/root/policy and materializes a unique 0600 file. The backend constructs argv and
    43	environment and owns process-group termination and cleanup. `build_command()` remains pure and
    44	vendor-specific.
    45	
    46	The argv is `[absolute_srt, "--settings", settings_path, "--", absolute_vendor, ...]` as
    47	documented by SRT. Options that weaken nested, network, Unix-socket, local-binding, or Apple Event
    48	isolation are never project-configurable.
    49	
    50	### D3 — Mode-aware filesystem policy
    51	
    52	Review and validation-shaped commands receive no project write roots. Alternative, quick,
    53	implementation, and documentation-shaped commands may write only the strict canonical worktree
    54	root. Every sandboxed command receives a backend-owned, per-launch state root used for HOME,
    55	XDG state/config/cache, and runtime temporary files. dg-07 sandbox lanes are eligible only when
    56	authentication is environment-backed; file-backed login state is denied and remains rollout-
    57	ineligible until dg-08 can broker it safely. Per-lane state variables and credential environment
    58	keys are authored in `agents.yaml`; no renderer hard-codes a vendor. The root must exist, equal `git
    59	rev-parse --show-toplevel`, pass the existing `checkout_policy.py` managed-worktree check, and
    60	must not be `/`, the user's home, or the shared checkout.
    61	
    62	The worktree `.git` pointer and linked-worktree common Git metadata are explicitly denied for
    63	writes. A sandboxed worker may edit files but skill prompts do not ask it to commit; the host
    64	orchestrator validates and creates the save-point commit after collecting the worker result. This
    65	avoids granting one agent write access to shared objects and refs.
    66	Symlink escapes are rejected/tested; hardlink aliasing is measured and documented as a residual
    67	same-user risk rather than overstated as contained.
    68	
    69	Reads deny the platform user-home region (`/home` on Linux, `/Users` on macOS) and explicitly
    70	re-allow only the canonical worktree, read-only common Git metadata, pinned runtime/tool paths,
    71	and authored credential-free inputs. Named credential paths and sibling checkouts remain denied.
    72	System/runtime reads outside the user-home region are a documented residual. Tests cover `git
    73	status` readability, denied Git mutation, credential/sibling/arbitrary-home reads, and the
    74	read-only common-git carve-out.
    75	
    76	### D4 — Exact-agent, default-deny network export
    77	
    78	The coordinator exports a snapshot from the exact agent's profile assignment plus global rules.
    79	The snapshot uses a closed SRT-compatible hostname plus separately range-checked port grammar,
    80	explicit scope and priority, schema revision, and canonical SHA-256 digest. Migration 044 adds
    81	`updated_at` and an atomic exact-agent export function; `policy_revision` is
    82	`v1:<maximum-updated-at-UTC>:<row-count>`. `policy_digest` is SHA-256 over UTF-8 canonical JSON
    83	(lexicographically sorted object keys, preserved rule-array order, no insignificant whitespace,
    84	no floats), excluding the digest field itself.
    85	Disabled rules are absent.
    86	
    87	SRT's deny-first semantics cannot represent every ordered SQL policy exactly. Rendering therefore
    88	keeps every applicable deny and only authored allows; conflicts become narrower. New writes are
    89	validated against the export grammar. Any legacy malformed applicable rule makes the entire export
    90	unrenderable; rules are never silently omitted. Malformed or unavailable export fails closed before
    91	vendor launch; it never becomes a fail-open reason or a synthetic destination list. An authored,
    92	successfully exported empty allow set remains a valid deny-all policy. A default-allow snapshot is
    93	not renderable by this backend and fails closed. The
    94	export contract is authoritative for sandbox execution; the older advisory SQL matcher is not used
    95	to construct SRT settings. Renderer tests pin SRT 0.0.77 wildcard apex/multi-label behavior and
    96	prove every rendered allow is a subset of the authored effective policy. DNS names, IPv4 literals,
    97	and bracketed IPv6 literals are supported; CIDR belongs only to denied-resolved-address policy and
    98	is not accepted as a destination rule.
    99	
   100	Provider endpoints are not hard-coded in the renderer. Current seed policy lacks several vendor
   101	API domains, so dg-07 does not flip existing local lanes to `sandbox`; rollout requires an
   102	authored endpoint inventory and a successful preflight. The controlled acceptance CLI exercises
   103	enforcement independently of production vendor endpoints.
   104	
   105	The autopilot `local` provider is rollout-ineligible under `sandbox` until its authored hostname
   106	and port are exportable, its Node client is proven to use SRT's proxy path, and SRT supports the
   107	destination class. Loopback, link-local, private-IP, or mDNS rejection is a fail-closed
   108	policy/capability outcome, never a fail-open reason.
   109	
   110	### D5 — Sanitize boundary-shaping environment, do not claim secret brokering
   111	
   112	The environment passed to SRT itself removes uppercase/lowercase `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`,
   113	`ALL_PROXY`, and `NO_PROXY`; `NODE_OPTIONS`; `LD_PRELOAD`, `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`,
   114	`DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`, `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH`; `PYTHONPATH`, `PYTHONHOME`, `PYTHONSTARTUP`,
   115	`RUBYOPT`, `RUBYLIB`, `PERL5OPT`, `PERL5LIB`, `BASH_ENV`, and `ENV`; Git directory, worktree,
   116	index, object, alternate-object, and config override variables; and `TMPDIR`, `TEMP`, and `TMP`.
   117	SRT may then author the proxy variables its child needs. This prevents an ambient parent proxy
   118	from bypassing address checks. The unsandboxed compatibility path retains the caller's original
   119	environment byte for byte. Runtime discovery records absolute Node, SRT entrypoint, `bwrap`,
   120	`socat`, and `rg` paths and constructs PATH from their parents, fixed root-owned non-writable
   121	system directories, and explicitly configured tool directories inside the canonical worktree;
   122	vendor executables are absolute and inherited descriptors are closed. Environment-backed vendor
   123	credentials remain readable by the vendor process; dg-08 owns request-time substitution and the
   124	downstream sandboxed-harness change owns broader credential brokering.
   125	
   126	### D6 — Narrow fail-open with durable evidence
   127	
   128	Only unsupported OS, missing/incompatible pinned runtime, or failed pre-launch capability probe
   129	may run the original command. The backend first writes a durable coordinator event; if unavailable,
   130	it appends a caller-generated stable `event_id` and fsyncs canonical JSONL under
   131	`${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/agentic-coding-tools/sandbox-events/outbox.jsonl`, with a 0700
   132	parent, 0600 file, advisory lock, and directory fsync. The state root must be absolute,
   133	operator-owned, no-follow/no-symlink, and outside every checkout; relative, wrong-owner,
   134	checkout-contained, or symlinked roots fail closed. It is never exposed as sandbox-writable.
   135	Failure of both blocks dispatch. Unsafe root,
   136	unrenderable policy, materialization failure, and all post-SRT-start failures fail closed.
   137	
   138	Each later event attempt drains older outbox entries before writing the new one, removing a record
   139	only after the endpoint acknowledges its `event_id`. Compaction holds the lock, writes a
   140	same-directory 0600 temporary file, fsyncs it, atomically replaces the outbox, and fsyncs the
   141	directory. Migration 044 makes `event_id` unique; replay returns the original durable audit row id.
   142	Only connection failures, timeouts, and 5xx responses may use or retain the outbox. Authentication,
   143	authorization, and schema 4xx failures on a live event fail closed. A permanently rejected queued
   144	record moves atomically to a mode-0600 dead-letter file with its response metadata, then drain
   145	continues; it is never silently deleted or allowed to block all later evidence. Audit payloads
   146	contain key names and digests, never prompt/argv bodies, settings bodies, or secret values.
   147	
   148	### D7 — Pin and probe SRT
   149	
   150	The repository pins `@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime` 0.0.77 with lockfile integrity and Node
   151	>=20.11.0. `install.sh` and CI may run `npm ci` in the primary checkout's
   152	`tools/sandbox-runtime`; dispatch performs no installation. Discovery order is an explicit
   153	absolute override, then the primary checkout derived from `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, then
   154	unavailable. Linked worktrees therefore use one pinned ignored installation rather than looking
   155	for their own `node_modules`; runtime copies never resolve relative to `__file__`. The backend
   156	launches the absolute Node binary and pinned absolute SRT JS entrypoint only after the package
   157	version and exact package-lock resolved URL/integrity entry match installed metadata. Versions before
   158	0.0.16 are forbidden by the official network-escape advisory.
   159	
   160	Linux preflight checks `bwrap`, `socat`, `rg`, supported architecture/seccomp conditions,
   161	user-namespace/AppArmor viability, and a no-op sandbox launch. macOS checks the Seatbelt backend,
   162	`sandbox-exec`, violation reporting, and a no-op launch. This host currently lacks `socat` and restricts unprivileged user
   163	namespaces, so real enforcement evidence must run on a capable host; local tests must report the
   164	skip reason, never manufacture a pass.
   165	
   166	Sources:
   167	
   168	- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/blob/main/README.md
   169	- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/blob/main/package.json
   170	- https://github.com/anthropics/sandbox-runtime/security/advisories/GHSA-9gqj-5w7c-vx47
   171	
   172	### D8 — Backend coverage and timeout ownership
   173	
   174	Sync submit, async submit, poll, repair retry, read-only snapshot fallback, and autopilot local-provider
   175	launch all use the backend exactly once per process attempt. There is no cancellation subprocess
   176	today; any future configured cancellation command is covered by the same structural guard. The
   177	actual invocation cwd is the policy root. The backend returns a typed
   178	`prelaunch_enforcement_blocked` result. For polling, policy outage or another prelaunch enforcement
   179	failure is a retryable collection condition until the existing poll deadline and then becomes
   180	`remote_state_unknown`; it must not close a still-running remote task as a vendor failure. Snapshot
   181	fallback is forbidden for write-capable modes because cleanup would discard edits. Read-only
   182	snapshot retries construct a new attempt context with the same routing digest and the snapshot
   183	execution root. On timeout the backend starts a new session, sends TERM to the
   184	process group, waits a bounded grace period, sends KILL if required, waits, and then cleans owned
   185	material. It never replays unsandboxed after process start. Cleanup failures emit durable
   186	`cleanup_status=failed` metadata with owned residual paths and block reuse of those paths; cleanup
   187	claims are never manufactured.
   188	
   189	### D9 — Ownership relative to sandboxed-harness execution
   190	
   191	dg-07 owns the local process seam, local SRT backend, network export, and sandbox execution audit.
   192	`add-sandboxed-harness-execution` consumes them and retains cloud backends, credential brokering,
   193	and trust-gate coupling. Its duplicate local-backend/export task groups are reconciled after dg-07
   194	lands.
   195	
   196	### D10 — Applicability is explicit
   197	
   198	dg-07 enforces local CLI processes. A routed sandbox assignment is authoritative over
   199	`agents.yaml`; YAML mode/entry fallback is consulted only for standalone calls. SDK, Agent-tool,
   200	and cloud-worker lanes do not traverse this backend and must not emit a fake local-SRT event or
   201	claim dg-07 enforcement; their containment evidence remains a harness/downstream contract.
   202	Sandbox execution events are emitted only when
   203	`requested_isolation=sandbox`; `none` and `worktree` retain their no-coordinator compatibility
   204	path. `enforcement_scope=execution` means the wrapped process performs the work locally;
   205	`submission` covers local submit and poll CLIs for remote work.
   206	
   207	## Validation strategy
   208	
   209	Tests begin RED at each contract boundary. Unit and integration tests cover decision immutability,
   210	policy normalization, deterministic rendering, root validation, environment stripping, hostile
   211	argv, durable degradation, cleanup, and every subprocess sink. A static AST guard prevents new
   212	vendor process launches outside the backend.
   213	
   214	A capability-gated real-runtime test must demonstrate read/write and egress restrictions from a
   215	linked worktree and run at least one configured real vendor executable through the same backend.
   216	A pull-request-triggered GitHub Actions matrix uses `ubuntu-24.04` (with the documented AppArmor
   217	user-namespace setup) and `macos-14`; each supported backend family must pass before its lanes are
   218	rollout-eligible. Jobs upload `sandbox-runtime-evidence.json`; the validator uses `gh run view` and
   219	`gh run download` and verifies conclusion, workflow path, head SHA, platform, artifact digest, and
   220	run id before the checked-in completion record is accepted at
   221	at `openspec/changes/add-dispatch-sandbox-enforcement/evidence/sandbox-runtime-evidence.json` and
   222	includes workflow/run identity. The gate reports `unsupported` with exact prerequisites on an
   223	incapable host; roadmap completion requires both supported backend-family passes.
   224	
   225	## Residual risks
   226	
   227	- A permitted destination such as GitHub remains an exfiltration channel.
   228	- A child can read credentials intentionally supplied to it.
   229	- Hardlinks and same-user races may exceed path-only containment.
   230	- SRT is pre-1.0 and its config may change; the exact pin and renderer tests bound that risk.
     1	## ADDED Requirements
     2	
     3	### Requirement: Network policy SHALL be exportable for one exact agent
     4	
     5	The coordinator SHALL export the enabled global rules plus the exact agent's profile-specific
     6	rules as a versioned, deterministic, default-deny document. Each export SHALL carry the exact
     7	agent id, normalized ordered rules, schema revision, and canonical content digest. Any malformed
     8	applicable legacy rule SHALL make the whole export unrenderable; rules SHALL NOT be silently
     9	omitted. The digest SHALL cover canonical UTF-8 JSON for every snapshot field except the digest
    10	itself, and applied execution events SHALL copy the exact revision and digest they enforced.
    11	
    12	The authenticated principal MAY export its own policy. Exporting another agent's policy requires
    13	trust level 3 or greater so the dispatch host can prepare a child without granting arbitrary agents
    14	cross-agent policy discovery.
    15	
    16	#### Scenario: Exact-agent export preserves authored rules
    17	
    18	WHEN an agent has profile-specific and global network rules
    19	THEN export SHALL include only that profile's enabled rules and enabled global rules
    20	AND profile-specific precedence and authored priority SHALL be explicit.
    21	
    22	#### Scenario: Rendering never widens policy
    23	
    24	WHEN authored precedence cannot be represented exactly by SRT deny-first semantics
    25	THEN the exported rules SHALL render to a conservative narrower result
    26	AND no destination absent from the authored effective policy SHALL be introduced.
    27	
    28	#### Scenario: Policy outage denies network
    29	
    30	WHEN an exact-agent export is unavailable or malformed at cold start
    31	THEN sandbox preparation SHALL fail closed before vendor process start
    32	AND SHALL NOT synthesize a destination list or treat the outage as fail-open.
    33	
    34	### Requirement: Sandbox execution events SHALL be durably auditable
    35	
    36	The coordinator SHALL accept a narrow sandbox execution event and SHALL not acknowledge durable
    37	success until the audit row is inserted. `event_id` SHALL be generated once by the caller, remain
    38	stable through outbox replay, and be an idempotency key; replay SHALL return the original audit row
    39	id and `replayed=true`. Events SHALL include routing correlation and full-context digest, execution location and
    40	scope, requested and applied isolation, runtime/preflight outcome, policy revision/digest,
    41	canonical root, executable paths, allowed environment key names, and degradation reason without
    42	secret values.
    43	
    44	The server SHALL author `created_at`. `sandbox_applied=true` SHALL require the SRT backend,
    45	successful preflight, non-null runtime/policy/settings/root evidence, and no degradation reason.
    46	`sandbox_applied=false` SHALL require a degradation reason. Cleanup failure SHALL carry residual
    47	owned paths.
    48	
    49	The request's `agent_id` names the target CLI lane; the audit actor SHALL be derived from the
    50	authenticated principal and SHALL NOT be accepted from request JSON. Recording an event for
    51	another agent requires trust level 3 or greater.
    52	
    53	#### Scenario: Durable degradation event precedes fallback
    54	
    55	WHEN sandbox preflight permits an unsandboxed fallback
    56	THEN the coordinator SHALL persist `applied=false` before acknowledging the event
    57	AND the fallback process SHALL not start before acknowledgement or a durable local outbox write.
    58	
    59	#### Scenario: Permanent outbox rejection does not poison later evidence
    60	
    61	WHEN an older queued event receives a permanent 4xx response during drain
    62	THEN that record SHALL move atomically to a durable dead-letter file with response metadata
    63	AND later queued records MAY continue draining
    64	AND a live event receiving 4xx SHALL fail closed rather than enter the outbox.
    65	
    66	#### Scenario: Secret values are excluded
    67	
    68	WHEN a sandbox execution event is persisted
    69	THEN environment metadata SHALL contain key names only
    70	AND argv prompt bodies, credential values, and settings-file contents SHALL be absent.
     1	## ADDED Requirements
     2	
     3	### Requirement: Local vendor CLI execution SHALL use one enforcement backend
     4	
     5	Every local vendor CLI lifecycle command SHALL pass through one shared process backend. This
     6	includes synchronous execution, asynchronous submission, asynchronous polling, and the autopilot
     7	local-provider harness. Discovery and health probes are control-plane operations and are explicitly
     8	excluded. No cancellation subprocess exists today; any future configured vendor cancellation
     9	command SHALL use the same backend.
    10	
    11	#### Scenario: Every vendor lifecycle command uses the backend
    12	
    13	WHEN a configured local vendor CLI is submitted, polled, or run synchronously
    14	THEN exactly one shared backend invocation SHALL own process creation
    15	AND a structural guard SHALL reject new direct vendor subprocess sinks.
    16	
    17	#### Scenario: Non-sandbox behavior remains compatible
    18	
    19	WHEN effective isolation is `none` or `worktree`
    20	THEN the backend SHALL preserve argv, stdin, cwd, timeout, and result behavior
    21	AND no sandbox settings file SHALL be created.
    22	
    23	### Requirement: Enforcement SHALL consume the immutable routing decision
    24	
    25	The backend SHALL consume the dg-06 enforcement projection and canonical full-context digest
    26	attached to dispatch context and SHALL NOT call routing again. Payload v2 SHALL have one isolation
    27	authority: the embedded context. A standalone caller without routed context SHALL resolve dg-05's
    28	exact-lane fallback once at the adapter boundary and record that provenance.
    29	
    30	#### Scenario: Routed execution is not re-resolved
    31	
    32	WHEN dispatch context carries a validated routing decision and isolation assignment
    33	THEN the same decision identifier, enforcement projection, and full-context digest SHALL appear in
    34	the execution audit
    35	AND no router request SHALL occur during rendering, preparation, or process execution.
    36	
    37	#### Scenario: Standalone dispatch resolves the exact lane
    38	
    39	WHEN a review-panel dispatch has no routed context
    40	THEN effective isolation SHALL be resolved from its exact agent id and dispatch mode
    41	AND an entry-level value SHALL be inherited only when that mode has no override.
    42	
    43	### Requirement: Sandbox rendering SHALL be pure and mode-aware
    44	
    45	The SRT renderer SHALL be deterministic and side-effect free. Review mode SHALL receive no project
    46	worktree write access. Write-capable modes MAY write only beneath a strictly resolved canonical Git
    47	worktree root. Per-launch vendor state SHALL be isolated from the operator's home. The user-home
    48	region SHALL be read-denied with narrow read-only worktree/common-Git/tool carve-outs. Credential
    49	files and sibling checkout reads SHALL remain denied; dg-07 sandbox rollout requires
    50	environment-backed authentication pending dg-08.
    51	
    52	#### Scenario: Review is read-only
    53	
    54	WHEN a `sandbox` decision is rendered for review
    55	THEN `filesystem.allowWrite` SHALL contain no project path
    56	AND an attempted project write inside or outside the worktree SHALL fail
    57	AND only the backend-owned ephemeral state root and SRT's documented internal paths MAY remain
    58	writable.
    59	
    60	#### Scenario: Write-capable work is root-confined
    61	
    62	WHEN a `sandbox` decision is rendered for an alternative or quick dispatch
    63	THEN the only project write root SHALL be the canonical worktree root
    64	AND the worktree `.git` pointer and common Git metadata SHALL be denied for writes
    65	AND writes through path or symlink escapes SHALL fail.
    66	
    67	#### Scenario: User-home reads are confined
    68	
    69	WHEN a sandboxed vendor process reads the canonical worktree and linked-worktree Git metadata
    70	THEN those reads SHALL succeed
    71	AND reads of a credential fixture, sibling checkout, or unrelated user-home file SHALL fail.
    72	
    73	#### Scenario: Rendering has no effects
    74	
    75	WHEN identical validated context and policy inputs are rendered twice
    76	THEN the policy documents and digests SHALL be identical
    77	AND rendering SHALL NOT write files, spawn processes, or contact a service.
    78	
    79	### Requirement: Prepared sandbox commands SHALL own lifecycle and truthful state
    80	
    81	The impure preparation layer SHALL own a unique mode-0600 settings file, sanitized child
    82	environment, absolute executable paths, process group, applied/degraded metadata, and cleanup.
    83	The wrapped argv SHALL separate SRT options from the vendor argv with `--`.
    84	
    85	#### Scenario: Concurrent launches do not share policy material
    86	
    87	WHEN two sandboxed commands are prepared concurrently
    88	THEN each SHALL receive a distinct settings path
    89	AND success, failure, and timeout SHALL remove only that command's material.
    90	
    91	#### Scenario: Timeout terminates the complete process tree
    92	
    93	WHEN a sandboxed vendor command exceeds its timeout
    94	THEN the backend SHALL terminate its process group, wait, escalate if required, and clean up
    95	AND no child process, listener, settings file, or owned mount artifact SHALL remain.
    96	
    97	#### Scenario: Execution metadata is truthful
    98	
    99	WHEN a sandbox was requested but not applied
   100	THEN result and audit metadata SHALL report `requested=sandbox` and `applied=false`
   101	AND the dispatch SHALL NOT describe itself as sandboxed.
   102	
   103	### Requirement: Degradation SHALL be narrow, durable, and pre-launch
   104	
   105	Sandbox execution events SHALL be emitted only for requested `sandbox` isolation. Unsandboxed
   106	fallback SHALL occur only for a preflight-proven unsupported platform, absent or
   107	incompatible pinned runtime, or failed platform capability probe. A warning and durable audit or
   108	outbox event SHALL exist before launch. Unsafe roots, malformed policies, and audit persistence
   109	failure SHALL fail closed. Malformed or unavailable policy SHALL fail before process start; an
   110	authored valid empty-allow policy remains a usable deny-all sandbox. No post-launch sandbox
   111	failure SHALL be retried unsandboxed.
   112	
   113	#### Scenario: Missing runtime degrades visibly
   114	
   115	WHEN isolation is `sandbox` and the pinned runtime is absent
   116	THEN a durable `applied=false` event SHALL be recorded before the original command starts
   117	AND the command MAY proceed unsandboxed with a warning.
   118	
   119	#### Scenario: Audit failure blocks fail-open
   120	
   121	WHEN neither coordinator audit persistence nor the local durable outbox succeeds
   122	THEN the unsandboxed vendor command SHALL NOT start.
   123	
   124	#### Scenario: Poll enforcement failure does not abandon remote work
   125	
   126	WHEN an asynchronous poll is blocked before its vendor process starts by sandbox enforcement
   127	THEN the collector SHALL retain the remote task and retry until its existing deadline
   128	AND SHALL NOT classify the remote vendor task itself as failed
   129	AND deadline exhaustion SHALL record `remote_state_unknown`, not terminal vendor failure.
   130	
   131	#### Scenario: Runtime failure never duplicates work
   132	
   133	WHEN SRT has started and exits nonzero or times out
   134	THEN the backend SHALL return that failure
   135	AND SHALL NOT retry the vendor command without the sandbox.
   136	
   137	### Requirement: The runtime dependency SHALL be pinned and probed
   138	
   139	The supported SRT package version and integrity SHALL be committed. Dispatch SHALL never install a
   140	runtime. Runtime selection SHALL validate package metadata, Node's version floor, platform
   141	dependencies, and a no-op launch before reporting `applied=true`.
   142	
   143	#### Scenario: Incompatible runtime is not trusted
   144	
   145	WHEN an executable named `srt` is present but its package metadata does not match the pin
   146	THEN the preflight SHALL classify it as incompatible
   147	AND degradation SHALL follow the durable pre-launch path.
   148	
   149	#### Scenario: Known network-escape versions are rejected
   150	
   151	WHEN the detected package version is older than 0.0.16
   152	THEN it SHALL never be used for network enforcement.

     1	# Design: Pin the isolation contract between router and dispatch
     2	
     3	## Decision D1 — One pure module serves both runtime paths
     4	
     5	`agent-coordinator/src/isolation_contract.py` is the one definition of
     6	`none`, `worktree`, and `sandbox`. It is stdlib-only and exports the static
     7	type, allowed values, `IsolationContractError`, validation, an
     8	`IsolationResolution(value, source)` result, and a pure per-mode helper.
     9	
    10	The coordinator imports it normally. The coordinator-unreachable fallback
    11	loads the same file through its checkout-root import shim. Published dg-04
    12	schemas retain serialized enums, but parity tests derive expected values from
    13	D1 rather than hand-maintained runtime definitions.
    14	
    15	## Decision D2 — Resolution records absence, invalid values, and provenance
    16	
    17	The ladder is: a reachable router's present valid value (`source=router`); the
    18	matching configured agent's mode override then entry default
    19	(`source=agents_yaml`); and `none` (`source=default`). Absent values fall
    20	through. A present invalid value raises `IsolationContractError` naming the
    21	rung; empty values are never silently coerced with `or "none"`.
    22	
    23	`get_agent_isolation(agent_type, dispatch_mode=None, *, agent_id=None)` stays
    24	source-compatible. Router and fallback call sites that know identity supply it,
    25	preventing local/remote entries of the same type from depending on YAML order.
    26	
    27	## Decision D3 — Mode overrides apply before assignments are emitted
    28	
    29	`ModeConfig` gains optional `isolation`. `vendor_registry` exposes mode-aware
    30	information and the resolver computes assignment isolation after dispatch mode
    31	is known. The fallback uses the same helper before filtering or sorting a lane.
    32	Dispatch-config projection and the skills review dispatcher parse the additive
    33	field. dg-06 execution wiring and dg-07 enforcement remain excluded.
    34	
    35	## Decision D4 — Widening requires an explicit amendment
    36	
    37	`container` is not valid in this change. Before
    38	`add-sandboxed-harness-execution` can introduce that posture, a future OpenSpec
    39	amendment must update the canonical type and values, both published schema
    40	enums, validation and precedence tests, and the router/fallback parity matrix.
    41	Until that amendment lands, every producer and consumer rejects `container`
    42	as an invalid present value rather than treating it as absence or `none`.
     1	## ADDED Requirements
     2	
     3	### Requirement: The isolation vocabulary SHALL be specified once and referenced by both producer and consumer
     4	
     5	The isolation vocabulary — `none`, `worktree`, and `sandbox` — SHALL be defined in exactly one location, and both the task router that emits an isolation value and the dispatch layer that consumes it SHALL reference that definition rather than restating the value set.
     6	
     7	The router already emits an isolation value and the dispatch layer already consumes one, but no artifact defines what the values mean. Two independent restatements of a vocabulary drift silently, and the first divergence is a dispatch that runs under a posture nobody intended.
     8	
     9	#### Scenario: Producer and consumer share one definition
    10	
    11	WHEN the task router emits an isolation value
    12	AND the dispatch layer resolves that value
    13	THEN both SHALL derive the accepted value set from the same definition
    14	AND neither SHALL hard-code an independent copy of the vocabulary.
    15	
    16	#### Scenario: Static contracts remain in parity with the canonical vocabulary
    17	
    18	WHEN the published routing OpenAPI or routing-policy schema is checked
    19	THEN its isolation enum SHALL equal the canonical vocabulary
    20	AND the check SHALL fail if either contract drifts from the runtime definition.
    21	
    22	#### Scenario: An unrecognized isolation value is rejected
    23	
    24	WHEN a value outside the defined vocabulary reaches the dispatch layer
    25	THEN resolution SHALL fail with an explicit error naming the offending value
    26	AND dispatch SHALL NOT proceed under a silently substituted posture.
    27	
    28	### Requirement: Isolation resolution SHALL follow a documented precedence ladder
    29	
    30	Effective isolation SHALL be resolved by a documented precedence ladder: the task router when it is reachable, then `get_agent_isolation()` reading `agents.yaml`, then `none`.
    31	
    32	This mirrors the precedence structure already established for execution-environment detection, so that one mental model covers both.
    33	
    34	#### Scenario: Router value wins when the router is reachable
    35	
    36	WHEN the task router is reachable
    37	AND it returns an isolation value for the dispatch
    38	THEN that value SHALL be the effective isolation
    39	AND `agents.yaml` SHALL NOT override it.
    40	
    41	#### Scenario: agents.yaml supplies the value when the router is silent
    42	
    43	WHEN the task router is reachable but returns no isolation value for the dispatch
    44	THEN `get_agent_isolation()` SHALL supply the effective isolation from `agents.yaml`.
    45	
    46	#### Scenario: Coordinator-unreachable yields a decision, not an error
    47	
    48	WHEN the coordinator is unreachable
    49	THEN resolution SHALL yield a defined isolation decision rather than raising
    50	AND the decision SHALL fall through to `agents.yaml`, then to `none`
    51	AND the resolved decision SHALL record which rung of the ladder produced it.
    52	
    53	#### Scenario: Absence falls through
    54	
    55	WHEN a reachable router supplies no isolation value
    56	OR a configured agent has no matching per-mode override
    57	THEN resolution SHALL fall through to the next rung and record that source.
    58	
    59	#### Scenario: Invalid presence fails closed
    60	
    61	WHEN any supplied isolation value is outside the canonical vocabulary
    62	THEN resolution SHALL raise an explicit contract error naming the source rung
    63	AND SHALL NOT treat that invalid value as an absent value.
    64	
    65	
    66	### Requirement: Isolation SHALL resolve for an (agent_type, dispatch_mode) pair
    67	
    68	Effective isolation SHALL resolve for an `(agent_type, dispatch_mode)` pair rather than for an agent type alone, and `agents.yaml` SHALL be able to express a per-mode override within a single agent entry.
    69	
    70	`agents.yaml` already implies per-mode postures — a `review` mode carrying read-only flags beside an `alternative` mode carrying write flags — and today cannot express the difference.
    71	
    72	#### Scenario: Review and alternative modes resolve differently under one entry
    73	
    74	WHEN one agent entry declares a per-mode isolation override for `review`
    75	AND the same entry declares a different posture for `alternative`
    76	THEN resolving `(agent_type, "review")` SHALL return the review posture
    77	AND resolving `(agent_type, "alternative")` SHALL return the alternative posture.
    78	
    79	#### Scenario: Entry-level posture applies when no per-mode override exists
    80	
    81	WHEN an agent entry declares an isolation posture with no per-mode override
    82	THEN every dispatch mode for that entry SHALL resolve to the entry-level posture.
    83	
    84	#### Scenario: Exact agent identity disambiguates repeated agent types
    85	
    86	WHEN more than one `agents.yaml` entry has the same agent type
    87	AND the resolver is given the dispatched agent identity
    88	THEN its per-mode or entry-level posture SHALL be resolved from that exact entry
    89	AND SHALL NOT depend on YAML ordering.
    90	
    91	#### Scenario: Router and local fallback agree on a configured mode override
    92	
    93	WHEN an agent entry defines a per-mode isolation override
    94	AND both paths select that agent and mode
    95	THEN both paths SHALL emit the same effective isolation value.

     1	# Design: Make the orchestrator obey the router
     2	
     3	## Decision D1 — Routing is injected at the host seam
     4	
     5	The roadmap state machine accepts a routing resolver protocol and invokes it before
     6	every synchronous `execute_roadmap` host dispatch. The resolver is responsible for bridge/coordinator access; the
     7	state machine never imports a vendor SDK or executes a model directly. Legacy callers
     8	may omit the resolver during migration, but a configured resolver fails closed when it
     9	is unavailable, raises, or returns malformed data.
    10	
    11	## Decision D2 — Dispatch context is immutable and versioned
    12	
    13	Every routed attempt carries schema version 1, the router's durable `decision_id`, the
    14	roadmap item and phase, an attempt number, a dispatch/ledger work ID, and the complete
    15	selected assignment. Canonical isolation is copied to the host envelope as one of
    16	`none`, `worktree`, or `sandbox`. The state machine validates and deep-copies this
    17	context so host code cannot mutate the router's decision in place.
    18	
    19	## Decision D3 — Completion must prove the active routed attempt
    20	
    21	A routed host result is terminal only when its proof echoes the durable active decision
    22	ID, dispatch work ID, observed agent ID, and expected ledger status. Completed work
    23	advances the phase. Capacity failures first persist the policy decision: WAIT preserves
    24	the lane and pause window, while SWITCH excludes the observed lane and requests a fresh
    25	router decision. Failed work closes the attempt and fails the item. Vendor-limit
    26	status, policy action, and any WAIT pause window are committed in one checkpoint save;
    27	a configured cost ceiling without authoritative routed cost evidence fails closed.
    28	The host-owned
    29	resolver/reconciler boundary supplies coordinator ledger evidence; the state machine
    30	validates that evidence against its checkpoint and never treats host mutation of the
    31	dispatch copy as authority. Retrying the same decision or accepting a stale,
    32	mismatched, unavailable, or unknown result fails closed.
    33	
    34	## Decision D4 — Loop safety is durable state
    35	
    36	The checkpoint records a global iteration count, a durable-progress fingerprint,
    37	consecutive no-progress count, and the most recent escalation. A durable item, phase,
    38	or ledger transition changes the fingerprint and resets the no-progress count. Hitting
    39	either configured cap checkpoints the escalation before execution parks, so restart
    40	cannot erase the guard or duplicate the escalation. Resumption requires an explicit
    41	host acknowledgement; prepared work is reconciled before any new submission, and a
    42	counter-based escalation parks again unless the host intentionally raises the relevant
    43	positive cap.
    44	
    45	## Decision D5 — Additive migration preserves current callers
    46	
    47	The opt-in delegated batch lifecycle is outside this change: it prepares requests and
    48	applies collected results through a distinct durable contract rather than invoking the
    49	synchronous phase `dispatch_fn` seam. Routing that lifecycle requires a separate change.
    50	
    51	The routing resolver and safety state are additive. Existing checkpoints deserialize
    52	with empty safety state, and callers without a resolver retain the current host-assisted
    53	path until the skill host wires the bridge. The new global iteration and no-progress
    54	guards intentionally bound both legacy and routed execution; legacy policies configured
    55	above the no-progress cap may park at the safety boundary first. Once a resolver is supplied, no implicit
    56	static route or unverified success is accepted.
     1	## ADDED Requirements
     2	
     3	### Requirement: Executed Routing Decisions
     4	
     5	`autopilot-roadmap` SHALL obtain and durably persist a validated routing decision before each synchronous `execute_roadmap` host dispatch. The immutable dispatch context SHALL include a decision identifier, selected agent/vendor/model/location, canonical dg-05 isolation, dispatch mode, and ledger work/attempt correlation. The host seam SHALL preserve this context unchanged; the state machine SHALL not call a model SDK or select a vendor locally.
     6	
     7	#### Scenario: Ledger-verified vendor switch
     8	
     9	WHEN a submitted attempt reports a vendor-limit result
    10	AND active roadmap policy authorizes switching lanes
    11	THEN the orchestrator SHALL resolve a fresh alternate assignment excluding the observed limited lane
    12	AND persist a new attempt before redispatching the same item and phase
    13	AND accept success only when the terminal VendorResultEnvelope/ledger completion matches that attempt's decision identifier and observed lane
    14	AND reject a stale, mismatched, or unavailable completion without treating the phase as complete.
    15	
    16	#### Scenario: Routed vendor limit honors wait policy
    17	
    18	WHEN a routed attempt reports a vendor-limit result
    19	AND active roadmap policy requires waiting
    20	THEN the orchestrator SHALL close the attempt as vendor-limited and persist `policy_action: wait`
    21	AND SHALL persist the vendor pause and reset window without resolving or dispatching an alternate lane.
    22	
    23	#### Scenario: Router unavailable
    24	
    25	WHEN no validated routing decision can be obtained from the configured resolver
    26	THEN the orchestrator SHALL use only a declared static fallback assignment with canonical isolation
    27	OR SHALL checkpoint a fail-closed escalation
    28	AND SHALL NOT dispatch with an un-routed context.
    29	
    30	### Requirement: Roadmap Loop Safety Caps
    31	
    32	The roadmap execution loop SHALL enforce durable global iteration and no-progress safeguards. Their counters and last durable-progress fingerprint SHALL be checkpointed before each dispatch and survive a resumed process.
    33	
    34	#### Scenario: Stuck dispatch trips the cap
    35	
    36	WHEN the configured iteration cap is reached or consecutive iterations produce no durable item, phase, or correlated-ledger transition
    37	THEN the loop SHALL checkpoint an explicit parked/escalated outcome and return it without continuing to dispatch.
    38	
    39	#### Scenario: Resume does not duplicate a submitted attempt
    40	
    41	WHEN a process stops after persisting a prepared attempt and before terminal completion
    42	THEN a resumed process SHALL reconcile the correlated ledger state before any new submission
    43	AND SHALL NOT issue a duplicate dispatch for that attempt.

     1	# Design: Isolation posture detection
     2	
     3	## Context
     4	
     5	The detector collapses filesystem workspace isolation and network restriction into one
     6	boolean. dg-07 needs those facts independently while current callers depend on
     7	`isolation_provided`.
     8	
     9	## Decisions
    10	
    11	### D1 — Nested factual booleans
    12	
    13	`IsolationPosture.filesystem` means the harness supplies a per-session workspace.
    14	`IsolationPosture.network` means it enforces restricted egress. Neither claims a
    15	containment strength.
    16	
    17	### D2 — Read and construction compatibility
    18	
    19	`EnvironmentProfile.isolation_provided` derives from `posture.filesystem`. The legacy
    20	constructor maps its boolean to filesystem and defaults network false. Supplying both
    21	forms is an error.
    22	
    23	### D3 — Signals prove only their own dimension
    24	
    25	Precedence is applied independently per dimension across explicit env, coordinator,
    26	heuristic, and default layers. Exact Claude/Codex cloud markers prove filesystem;
    27	`CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED` proves network. A higher filesystem result does not
    28	prevent a lower layer from resolving network, while a structured coordinator network
    29	value blocks a lower network heuristic. The canonical coordinator field is
    30	`isolation_posture`; malformed canonical data rejects that layer and never falls back
    31	to a simultaneously supplied legacy boolean.
    32	
    33	### D4 — Migrate only worktree decision points
    34	
    35	Worktree and merge entrypoints read `posture.filesystem`; other callers retain the
    36	compatibility property. Fallback imports expose the same surface and output is unchanged.
    37	
    38	## Failure and verification
    39	
    40	Unknown explicit values fall through. Malformed coordinator values do not coerce.
    41	Tests first pin the model and truth table, then subprocess behavior. Focused/full tests,
    42	Ruff, strict OpenSpec validation, and multi-vendor review gate landing.

     1	"""Provider-neutral autopilot phase dispatch adapters.
     2	
     3	Scope note for the built-in `local` adapter: its concurrency cap
     4	(``LOCAL_INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENCY``) is enforced **per process**, not host-wide.
     5	The gate is a :class:`threading.Semaphore` owned by this module, so N concurrent
     6	autopilot processes pointed at the same endpoint can each admit up to the cap —
     7	the endpoint may see N x cap simultaneous requests. Host-level admission control
     8	belongs to the serving stack in front of the GPU, not here.

    38	@dataclass
    39	class PhaseDispatchPayload:
    40	    schema_version: int
    41	    change_id: str
    42	    phase: str
    43	    provider: str
    44	    archetype: str | None
    45	    model: str | None
    46	    prompt: str
    47	    system_prompt: str | None
    48	    isolation: str | None
    49	    expected_outcomes: list[str]
    50	    agent_id: str | None = None
    51	
    52	    @classmethod
    53	    def from_dict(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> "PhaseDispatchPayload":
    54	        return cls(
    55	            schema_version=int(data.get("schema_version", 1)),
    56	            change_id=str(data["change_id"]),
    57	            phase=str(data["phase"]),
    58	            provider=str(data["provider"]),
    59	            archetype=data.get("archetype"),
    60	            model=data.get("model"),
    61	            prompt=str(data["prompt"]),
    62	            system_prompt=data.get("system_prompt"),
    63	            isolation=data.get("isolation"),
    64	            expected_outcomes=list(data.get("expected_outcomes") or []),
    65	            agent_id=data.get("agent_id"),
    66	        )
    67	
    68	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    69	        return asdict(self)
    70	
    71	
    72	@dataclass
    73	class PhaseDispatchResult:
    74	    schema_version: int = 1
    75	    outcome: str = "failed"
    76	    handoff_id: str = ""
    77	    provider: str = ""
    78	    model_used: str | None = None
    79	    dispatch_tier: str = "fallback"
    80	    warnings: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    81	    agent_id: str | None = None
    82	    error_class: str | None = None
    83	    capacity_scope: str | None = None
    84	    capacity_model: str | None = None
    85	    capacity_reset_at: str | None = None
    86	    capacity_retry_after_seconds: int | None = None
    87	
    88	    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    89	        return asdict(self)

    97	# --- local provider adapter (OpenSpec add-local-model-provider-tier, D2/D5) ---
    98	#
    99	# `local` launches the existing Pi coding-agent harness with its normal file and
   100	# command tools. A one-shot Pi extension registers the distinct `local` provider
   101	# against the operator-run OpenAI-compatible endpoint (llama-server / vLLM /
   102	# Ollama); stdlib urllib remains only for the bounded health probe.
   103	#
   104	# Environment contract:
   105	#   LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL       required to enable; http:// or https:// only;
   106	#                                  includes the API version prefix, e.g.
   107	#                                  "http://gx10.local:8080/v1"
   108	#   LOCAL_INFERENCE_API_KEY        optional bearer token
   109	#   LOCAL_INFERENCE_MAX_CONCURRENCY  optional, default 4, clamped to 64; excess
   110	#                                  dispatches queue (per process — see the module
   111	#                                  docstring)
   112	#
   113	# With LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL unset the provider is inert: dispatch returns the
   114	# same structured `fallback` result any unconfigured adapter returns, and no
   115	# network call is made (Rule 4 — safe default).
   116	_LOCAL_PROVIDER = "local"
   117	_LOCAL_DEFAULT_MAX_CONCURRENCY = 4
   118	# A process cannot usefully hold more in-flight local requests than this, and a
   119	# fat-fingered env value must not turn the gate into an unbounded thread farm.
   120	_LOCAL_MAX_MAX_CONCURRENCY = 64
   340	        return False
   341	
   342	    if not force:
   343	        cached = _cached_probe_verdict(base_url)
   344	        if cached is not None:
   345	            return cached
   346	
   347	    # Single-flight: concurrent cold callers collapse onto one probe.
   348	    with _local_probe_lock:
   349	        if not force:
   350	            cached = _cached_probe_verdict(base_url)
   351	            if cached is not None:
   352	                return cached
   353	        try:
   354	            _call_with_deadline(
   355	                lambda: _http_get_json(
   356	                    f"{base_url}/models",
   357	                    _local_headers(),
   358	                    _LOCAL_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   359	                ),
   360	                _LOCAL_PROBE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   361	            )
   362	            reachable = True
   363	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — any probe failure is unavailability
   364	            logger.debug("local health probe failed for %s: %s", base_url, exc)
   365	            reachable = False
   366	
   367	        with _local_state_lock:
   368	            _local_probe_cache = (
   369	                base_url,
   370	                reachable,
   371	                time.monotonic() + _LOCAL_PROBE_TTL_SECONDS,
   372	            )
   373	        return reachable

   376	def normalize_dispatch_result(
   377	    raw: Any,
   378	    payload: PhaseDispatchPayload,
   379	    dispatch_tier: str,
   380	) -> PhaseDispatchResult:
   381	    """Normalize tuple/dict adapter output into the contract result shape."""
   382	    warnings: list[str] = []
   383	    outcome: str | None = None
   384	    handoff_id: str | None = None
   385	    model_used = payload.model
   386	    error_class: str | None = None
   387	    capacity_scope: str | None = None
   388	    capacity_model: str | None = None
   389	    capacity_reset_at: str | None = None
   390	    capacity_retry_after_seconds: int | None = None
   391	
   392	    if isinstance(raw, tuple) and len(raw) == 2:
   393	        outcome, handoff_id = raw
   394	    elif isinstance(raw, dict):
   395	        outcome = raw.get("outcome")
   396	        handoff_id = raw.get("handoff_id")
   397	        model_used = raw.get("model_used", model_used)
   398	        error_class = raw.get("error_class")
   399	        capacity_scope = raw.get("capacity_scope")
   400	        capacity_model = raw.get("capacity_model")
   401	        capacity_reset_at = raw.get("capacity_reset_at")
   402	        capacity_retry_after_seconds = raw.get("capacity_retry_after_seconds")
   403	        raw_warnings = raw.get("warnings")
   404	        if isinstance(raw_warnings, list):
   405	            warnings = [str(item) for item in raw_warnings]
   406	
   407	    if not isinstance(outcome, str) or not outcome:
   408	        outcome = "failed"
   409	        warnings.append("adapter returned missing outcome")
   410	    if not isinstance(handoff_id, str) or not handoff_id:
   411	        digest = hashlib.sha256(
   412	            json.dumps(payload.to_dict(), sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
   413	        ).hexdigest()[:12]
   414	        handoff_id = f"{dispatch_tier}:{payload.provider}:{payload.phase}:{digest}"
   415	        warnings.append("adapter returned missing handoff_id")
   416	
   417	    return PhaseDispatchResult(
   418	        outcome=outcome,
   419	        handoff_id=handoff_id,
   420	        provider=payload.provider,
   421	        model_used=model_used,
   422	        dispatch_tier=dispatch_tier,
   423	        warnings=warnings,
   424	        agent_id=payload.agent_id,
   425	        error_class=error_class,
   426	        capacity_scope=capacity_scope,
   427	        capacity_model=capacity_model,
   428	        capacity_reset_at=capacity_reset_at,
   429	        capacity_retry_after_seconds=capacity_retry_after_seconds,
   430	    )

   432	
   433	def _fallback_result(
   434	    payload: PhaseDispatchPayload,
   435	    warning: str,
   436	) -> PhaseDispatchResult:
   437	    """The structured degradation every unconfigured adapter returns."""
   438	    return PhaseDispatchResult(
   439	        outcome="failed",
   440	        handoff_id=f"fallback:{payload.provider}:{payload.phase}",
   441	        provider=payload.provider,
   442	        model_used=payload.model,
   443	        dispatch_tier="fallback",
   444	        warnings=[warning],
   445	        agent_id=payload.agent_id,
   446	    )

   449	def _local_harness_prompt(payload: PhaseDispatchPayload) -> str:
   450	    """Build the phase prompt consumed by the tool-capable Pi agent harness."""
   451	    expected = ", ".join(payload.expected_outcomes) or "complete, failed"
   452	    result_contract = json.dumps(
   453	        {
   454	            "outcome": f"<one of: {expected}>",
   455	            "handoff_id": "<real handoff id>",
   456	        },
   457	        separators=(",", ":"),
   458	    )
   459	    sections = [
   460	        payload.system_prompt or "You are a focused phase agent.",
   461	        payload.prompt,
   462	        (
   463	            "Use the coding-agent tools to inspect files, run commands, and make "
   464	            "only the changes required by this phase. A text-only answer is not a "
   465	            "completed phase. Before finishing, write a durable handoff through the "
   466	            "configured coordinator handoff capability (or its documented local "
   467	            "fallback). Your final assistant message must be only this JSON shape: "
   468	            f"{result_contract}. Never invent or omit the handoff id."
   469	        ),
   470	    ]
   471	    return (chr(10) * 2).join(sections)

   474	def _run_local_agent_cli(
   475	    payload: PhaseDispatchPayload,
   476	) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
   477	    """Run Pi headlessly with the local endpoint registered as a provider."""
   478	    if not _LOCAL_PI_EXTENSION.is_file():
   479	        raise LocalAdapterError("local Pi provider extension is missing")
   480	    env = os.environ.copy()
   481	    env["LOCAL_INFERENCE_MODEL"] = payload.model or ""
   482	    command = [
   483	        "pi",
   484	        "-p",
   485	        "--provider",
   486	        "local",
   487	        "--model",
   488	        payload.model or "",
   489	        "--mode",
   490	        "json",
   491	        "--approve",
   492	        "--no-session",
   493	        "--extension",
   494	        str(_LOCAL_PI_EXTENSION),
   495	        _local_harness_prompt(payload),
   496	    ]
   497	    return subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603 -- fixed executable and list-form args
   498	        command,
   499	        capture_output=True,
   500	        text=True,
   501	        timeout=_LOCAL_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   502	        env=env,
   503	        check=False,
   504	    )

   507	def _assistant_text(message: Any) -> str | None:
   508	    """Extract assistant text from a Pi JSON-mode message payload."""
   509	    if not isinstance(message, dict) or message.get("role") != "assistant":
   510	        return None
   511	    content = message.get("content")
   512	    if isinstance(content, str):
   513	        return content
   514	    if isinstance(content, list):
   515	        parts = [
   516	            part["text"]
   517	            for part in content
   518	            if isinstance(part, dict) and isinstance(part.get("text"), str)
   519	        ]
   520	        return chr(10).join(parts) if parts else None
   521	    return None
   522	
   523	
   524	def _parse_local_harness_output(stdout: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
   525	    """Return the last explicit outcome and handoff id from Pi NDJSON."""
   526	    last_text: str | None = None
   527	    for line in stdout.splitlines():
   528	        try:
   529	            event = json.loads(line)
   530	        except json.JSONDecodeError:
   531	            continue
   532	        if not isinstance(event, dict):
   533	            continue
   534	        text = _assistant_text(event.get("message"))
   535	        if text:
   536	            last_text = text
   537	    if last_text is None:
   538	        return None
   539	    try:
   540	        parsed = json.loads(last_text)
   541	    except json.JSONDecodeError:
   542	        return None
   543	    if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
   544	        return None
   545	    outcome = parsed.get("outcome")
   546	    handoff_id = parsed.get("handoff_id")
   547	    if (
   548	        not isinstance(outcome, str)
   549	        or not outcome.strip()
   550	        or not isinstance(handoff_id, str)
   551	        or not handoff_id.strip()
   552	    ):
   553	        return None
   554	    return parsed
   555	
   556	
   557	def _local_runner(payload: PhaseDispatchPayload) -> dict[str, Any]:
   558	    """Run one capped tool-capable agent session against the local endpoint."""
   559	    gate = _local_gate()
   560	    if not gate.acquire(timeout=_LOCAL_GATE_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS):
   561	        raise LocalGateTimeout(
   562	            f"no local dispatch slot within {_LOCAL_GATE_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS}s"
   563	        )
   564	    try:
   565	        completed = _run_local_agent_cli(payload)
   566	    finally:
   567	        gate.release()
   568	
   569	    if completed.returncode != 0:
   570	        return {
   571	            "outcome": "failed",
   572	            "warnings": ["local agent harness exited non-zero"],
   573	        }
   574	    if len(completed.stdout.encode("utf-8")) > _LOCAL_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES:
   575	        raise LocalResponseTooLarge("local agent harness output exceeded byte budget")
   576	    result = _parse_local_harness_output(completed.stdout)
   577	    if result is None:
   578	        return {
   579	            "outcome": "failed",
   580	            "warnings": [
   581	                "local agent harness returned no explicit outcome and real handoff_id"
   582	            ],
   583	        }
   584	    if payload.expected_outcomes and result["outcome"] not in payload.expected_outcomes:
   585	        return {
   586	            "outcome": "failed",
   587	            "warnings": ["local agent harness returned an unexpected outcome"],
   588	        }
   589	    return result
   590	
   591	
   592	def _local_trust_boundary_warning(payload: PhaseDispatchPayload) -> str | None:
   593	    """Refusal reason when *payload*'s archetype may not be served by `local`.
   594	
   595	    Design D3 puts the trust boundary in the coordinator's resolver. This is the
   596	    adapter-side backstop for payloads that never went through it: an absent or
   597	    non-permitted archetype is refused here, before any request is built.
   598	    """
   599	    archetype = payload.archetype
   600	    permitted = ", ".join(sorted(_LOCAL_TRUSTED_ARCHETYPES))
   601	    if not isinstance(archetype, str) or not archetype:
   602	        return (
   603	            "payload carries no archetype, so the 'local' provider trust boundary "
   604	            f"cannot be satisfied (permitted: {permitted}); no dispatch attempted"
   605	        )
   606	    if archetype not in _LOCAL_TRUSTED_ARCHETYPES:
   607	        return (
   608	            f"archetype {archetype!r} is outside the 'local' provider trust "
   609	            f"boundary (permitted: {permitted}); no dispatch attempted"
   610	        )
   611	    return None
   612	
   613	
   614	def _dispatch_local(payload: PhaseDispatchPayload) -> PhaseDispatchResult:
   615	    """Dispatch through the built-in local adapter, degrading instead of raising."""
   616	    if _local_base_url() is None:
   617	        if _local_base_url_raw():
   618	            return _fallback_result(
   619	                payload,
   620	                "adapter unavailable for provider 'local': LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL "
   621	                "must be an http:// or https:// URL",
   622	            )
   623	        return _fallback_result(
   624	            payload,
   625	            "adapter unavailable for provider 'local': LOCAL_INFERENCE_BASE_URL is not set",
   626	        )
   627	    boundary = _local_trust_boundary_warning(payload)
   628	    if boundary is not None:
   629	        return _fallback_result(
   630	            payload, f"adapter unavailable for provider 'local': {boundary}"
   631	        )
   632	    if not payload.model:
   633	        return _fallback_result(
   634	            payload,
   635	            "adapter unavailable for provider 'local': no model resolved for this "
   636	            "phase; no dispatch attempted",
   637	        )
   638	    if not local_endpoint_available():
   639	        return _fallback_result(
   640	            payload,
   641	            "adapter unavailable for provider 'local': health probe failed for "
   642	            "the configured endpoint",
   643	        )
   644	    try:
   645	        raw = _local_runner(payload)
   646	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — a dead endpoint must not fail the phase
   647	        logger.debug("local dispatch failed", exc_info=True)
   648	        if _is_connection_error(exc):
   649	            # The cached "reachable" verdict is now suspect; make the next
   650	            # caller re-probe instead of retrying into a black hole.
   651	            invalidate_local_probe_cache()
   652	        return _fallback_result(
   653	            payload,
   654	            "adapter unavailable for provider 'local': dispatch failed "
   655	            f"({type(exc).__name__})",
   656	        )
   657	    return normalize_dispatch_result(raw, payload, "harness")
   658

   660	def _dry_run_result(payload: PhaseDispatchPayload) -> PhaseDispatchResult:
   661	    if payload.provider != "claude_code" and payload.model in _CLAUDE_ALIASES:
   662	        return PhaseDispatchResult(
   663	            outcome="failed",
   664	            handoff_id=f"dry-run:{payload.provider}:{payload.phase}:invalid-model",
   665	            provider=payload.provider,
   666	            model_used=payload.model,
   667	            dispatch_tier="dry_run",
   668	            agent_id=payload.agent_id,
   669	            warnings=[
   670	                f"Claude alias {payload.model!r} is not valid for provider {payload.provider!r}",
   671	            ],
   672	        )
   673	    if payload.provider == _LOCAL_PROVIDER:
   674	        # Dry run models the real decision path: a payload the adapter would
   675	        # refuse at the trust boundary must not dry-run "complete".
   676	        boundary = _local_trust_boundary_warning(payload)
   677	        if boundary is not None:
   678	            return PhaseDispatchResult(
   679	                outcome="failed",
   680	                handoff_id=f"dry-run:{payload.provider}:{payload.phase}:trust-boundary",
   330	    normalized = raw.strip()
   331	    if normalized == "claude":
   332	        return "claude_code"
   333	    return normalized or None
