   336	def _build_options(
   337	    phase: str,
   338	    state_dict: dict[str, Any],
   339	    *,
   340	    provider: str | None = None,
   341	) -> dict[str, Any]:
   342	    """Assemble sub-agent dispatch options for *phase*.
   343	
   344	    Resolution order (precedence high → low):
   345	      1. ``AUTOPILOT_PHASE_MODEL_OVERRIDE`` env var (D8) — sets ``model``
   346	         only; leaves ``system_prompt`` to the harness default.
   347	      2. Coordinator archetype resolution (D5) — sets both ``model`` and
   348	         ``system_prompt`` from the resolved archetype, and records the
   349	         archetype name in ``state_dict["_resolved_archetype"]`` so
   350	         ``make_phase_callback`` can propagate it to ``LoopState.phase_archetype``.
   351	      3. Bridge failure (D9) — leaves ``options`` without ``model`` /
   352	         ``system_prompt``; the harness default applies; phase still
   353	         dispatches normally.
   354	
   355	    ``isolation="worktree"`` is set independently for phases in
   356	    :data:`_WORKTREE_PHASES`.
   357	
   358	    Mutates *state_dict* by writing ``_resolved_archetype`` only on the
   359	    archetype-resolution path (path 2). The override path (path 1) does
   360	    NOT record an archetype because the operator's choice carries no
   361	    archetype semantics.
   362	    """
   363	    options: dict[str, Any] = {}
   364	    if phase in _WORKTREE_PHASES:
   365	        options["isolation"] = "worktree"
   366	
   367	    # Path 1: operator override
   368	    override = _check_phase_model_override(phase)
   369	    if override:
   370	        options["model"] = override
   371	        return options
   372	
   373	    # Path 2: coordinator archetype resolution
   374	    signals = _extract_signals_for_phase(phase, state_dict)
   375	    selected_provider = _selected_provider(provider)
   376	    resolved = coordination_bridge.try_resolve_archetype_for_phase(
   377	        phase,
   378	        signals,
   379	        provider=selected_provider,
   380	    )
   381	    if resolved is not None:
   382	        options["model"] = resolved["model"]
   383	        options["system_prompt"] = resolved["system_prompt"]
   384	        state_dict["_resolved_archetype"] = resolved["archetype"]
   385	        # The coordinator rewrites `provider` to the vendor that actually owns
   386	        # the selected model, because adaptive routing ranks the whole catalog
   387	        # and may cross vendors. Taking `model` without `provider` produces a
   388	        # pair no adapter can dispatch -- provider="codex" with
   389	        # model="qwen/qwen3-coder". Optional passthrough, like write_capable:
   390	        # older coordinators omit it, and then the static provider stands.
   990	
   991	def build_phase_dispatch_kwargs(
   992	    phase: str,
   993	    change_id: str,
   994	    provider: str | None = None,
   995	    agent_id: str | None = None,
   996	) -> dict[str, Any]:
   997	    """Return the dispatch payload for a phase sub-agent (D3).
   998	
   999	    Side effect: writes ``openspec/changes/<change_id>/.phase-resolution-cache.json``
  1000	    so :func:`apply_phase_outcome` can later propagate the resolved
  1001	    archetype into ``LoopState.phase_archetype``.
  1002	
  1003	    Args:
  1004	        phase: Phase id (e.g. "IMPLEMENT", "PLAN_ITERATE").
  1005	        change_id: OpenSpec change identifier. Must match
  1006	            ``^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$`` (raises ``ValueError``
  1007	            otherwise — before any filesystem access).
  1008	
  1009	    Returns:
  1010	        ``{prompt, model, system_prompt, isolation, archetype}``. ``prompt``
  1011	        is the **already-folded** final string SKILL.md passes verbatim
  1012	        to ``Agent(...)`` — no further concatenation in prose.
  1013	    """
  1014	    # Validation runs before any path construction to make path-traversal
  1015	    # attempts a hard fail rather than a partial side-effect.
  1016	    _validate_change_id(change_id)
  1017	
  1018	    state_dict = _read_state_dict(change_id)
  1019	    state_dict["change_id"] = change_id  # ensure available for signal extraction
  1020	    current_phase = state_dict.get("current_phase", phase)
  1021	    last_handoff_id = state_dict.get("last_handoff_id")
  1022	
  1023	    incoming = _hydrate_incoming_handoff(change_id, last_handoff_id, current_phase)
  1024	
  1025	    # _build_options writes _resolved_archetype into state_dict on the
  1026	    # archetype path; we read it back below to populate the cache.
  1027	    selected_provider = _selected_provider(provider)
  1028	    options = _build_options(phase, state_dict, provider=selected_provider)
  1029	    phase_prompt = _build_prompt(phase, state_dict, incoming, artifacts_manifest=None)
  1030	
  1031	    system_prompt = options.get("system_prompt")
  1032	    model = options.get("model")
  1033	    isolation = options.get("isolation")
  1034	    archetype = state_dict.get("_resolved_archetype")
  1035	    write_capable = state_dict.get("_resolved_write_capable")
  1036	    # Dispatch to the vendor that owns the model adaptive routing picked, not
  1037	    # the statically configured one. _build_options records this only when the
  1038	    # coordinator supplied it, so the static provider remains the fallback.
  1039	    dispatch_provider = state_dict.get("_resolved_provider") or selected_provider
  1040	
  1041	    if isinstance(system_prompt, str) and system_prompt:
  1042	        folded_prompt = f"{system_prompt}{_PROMPT_SEPARATOR}{phase_prompt}"
  1043	    else:
  1044	        folded_prompt = phase_prompt
  1045	
  1046	    # Cache write — atomic. Schema v1 per D4.
  1047	    cache_payload: dict[str, Any] = {
  1048	        "schema_version": 1,
  1049	        "change_id": change_id,
  1050	        "phase": phase,
  1051	        "archetype": archetype,
  1052	        "checksum": _checksum_for_cache(change_id, phase, archetype),
  1053	    }
  1054	    _atomic_write_json(_cache_path(change_id), cache_payload)
  1055	
  1056	    return {
  1057	        "schema_version": 1,
  1058	        "change_id": change_id,
  1059	        "phase": phase,
  1060	        "provider": dispatch_provider,
  1061	        "agent_id": agent_id,
  1062	        "prompt": folded_prompt,
  1063	        "model": model,
  1064	        "system_prompt": system_prompt,
  1065	        "isolation": isolation,
  1066	        "archetype": archetype,
  1067	        "write_capable": write_capable,
  1068	        "expected_outcomes": _expected_outcomes_for_phase(phase),
  1069	    }
  1070	
  1071	
  1072	def _expected_outcomes_for_phase(phase: str) -> list[str]:
  1073	    """Return allowed outcomes for a phase dispatch payload.
  1074	
  1075	    VAL_REVIEW's ``max_iter`` was missing here even though
  1076	    ``autopilot.TRANSITIONS["VAL_REVIEW"]`` has always allowed it (a
  1077	    pre-existing bug found by Codex review while adjudicating this exact
  1078	    dict, PR #592) -- a real max_iter claim had no matching Choice
  1079	    criterion, forcing an artificial disagreement in the phase-outcome
  1080	    shadow judgment (roadmap ri-07).
    70	    hardcoded model and dispatch to the endpoint anyway.
    71	    """
    72	
    73	
    74	def _smoke_phase(provider: str) -> str:
    75	    return _LOCAL_SMOKE_PHASE if provider == _LOCAL_PROVIDER else _DEFAULT_SMOKE_PHASE
    76	
    77	
    78	def _build_payload(
    79	    provider: str,
    80	    model_override: str | None,
    81	    *,
    82	    dry_run: bool = False,
    83	) -> PhaseDispatchPayload:
    84	    if provider != "claude_code" and model_override in _CLAUDE_ALIASES:
    85	        raise ProviderModelMappingError(provider, model_override or "")
    86	
    87	    phase = _smoke_phase(provider)
    88	    state = {
    89	        "loc_estimate": 25,
    90	        "write_allow": ["skills/autopilot/**"],
    91	        "dependencies": [],
    92	    }
    93	    options = phase_agent._build_options(  # noqa: SLF001 - canonical public bridge path
    94	        phase, state, provider=provider
    95	    )
    96	    archetype = state.get("_resolved_archetype")
    97	
    98	    if provider == _LOCAL_PROVIDER:
    99	        if dry_run:
   100	            # Offline fixture; nothing leaves the process.
   101	            archetype = archetype or _LOCAL_DRY_RUN_ARCHETYPE
   102	        elif not archetype:
   103	            raise LocalTrustBoundaryError(
   104	                f"the resolver returned no archetype for phase {phase} under "
   105	                f"provider 'local' (refusal or coordinator unavailable); "
   106	                f"permitted archetypes: {', '.join(sorted(_LOCAL_TRUSTED_ARCHETYPES))}. "
   107	                "No dispatch attempted."
   108	            )
   109	        if archetype not in _LOCAL_TRUSTED_ARCHETYPES:
   110	            raise LocalTrustBoundaryError(
   111	                f"archetype {archetype!r} (phase {phase}) is outside the 'local' "
   112	                f"provider trust boundary; permitted archetypes: "
   113	                f"{', '.join(sorted(_LOCAL_TRUSTED_ARCHETYPES))}. No dispatch attempted."
   114	            )
   115	
   116	    model = model_override or options.get("model")
   117	    if not model:
   118	        if provider == _LOCAL_PROVIDER and not dry_run:
   119	            # Unreachable in practice (a resolved archetype carries a model), but
   120	            # the invariant is explicit: real local mode never ships a hardcoded
   121	            # model to the endpoint.
   122	            raise LocalTrustBoundaryError(
   123	                f"the resolver returned no model for phase {phase} under provider "
   124	                "'local'. No dispatch attempted."
   125	            )
   126	        model = _FALLBACK_MODELS.get(provider, _DEFAULT_FALLBACK_MODEL)
   127	    if provider != "claude_code" and model in _CLAUDE_ALIASES:
   128	        raise ProviderModelMappingError(provider, model)
   129	
   130	    incoming = PhaseRecord(
   131	        change_id="vendor-neutral-autopilot-smoke",
   132	        phase_name="smoke",
   133	        agent_type="autopilot",
   134	        summary="dry-run provider dispatch smoke",
   135	    )
   136	    prompt = phase_agent._build_prompt(  # noqa: SLF001 - smoke uses canonical helper
   137	        phase,
   138	        {"change_id": "vendor-neutral-autopilot-smoke", "current_phase": phase},
   139	        incoming,
   140	        # Synthetic, to match the synthetic change_id above. `_build_prompt`
   141	        # only renders manifest entries as prompt text and never opens them, so
   142	        # this was a stale label rather than a broken read — but it named a real
   143	        # change (archived 2026-05-16) beside a smoke id that is deliberately
   144	        # fictional, which is the inconsistency the stability guard exists to
   145	        # catch. Fixtures use synthetic ids precisely so they stay
   146	        # distinguishable from paths something actually reads.
   147	        artifacts_manifest=[
   148	            "openspec/changes/vendor-neutral-autopilot-smoke/design.md"
   149	        ],
   150	    )
   151	    system_prompt = options.get("system_prompt")
   152	    if system_prompt:
   153	        prompt = f"{system_prompt}{phase_agent._PROMPT_SEPARATOR}{prompt}"  # noqa: SLF001
   154	
   155	    return PhaseDispatchPayload(
   156	        schema_version=1,
   157	        change_id="vendor-neutral-autopilot-smoke",
   158	        phase=phase,
   159	        provider=provider,
   160	        archetype=archetype,
   161	        model=model,
   162	        prompt=prompt,
   163	        system_prompt=system_prompt,
   164	        isolation=options.get("isolation"),
   165	        expected_outcomes=["complete", "failed"],
   166	    )
   167

    46	        self,

    48	        agent_id: str | None = None,
    49	    ) -> AccessDecision:
    50	        """Check if an agent is allowed to access a domain.

     1	"""Audit trail service for Agent Coordinator.
     2	
     3	Provides immutable, async logging of all coordination operations.
     4	Audit entries are append-only — the database enforces immutability via triggers.
     5	"""
     6	
     7	import asyncio
     8	import logging
     9	import time
    10	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    11	from datetime import datetime
    12	from typing import Any
    13	
    14	from .config import get_config
    15	from .db import DatabaseClient, get_db
    16	
    17	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    18

    20	@dataclass
    21	class AuditEntry:
    22	    """Represents an audit log entry."""
    23

    53	            created_at=created_at,
    54	            delegated_from=data.get("delegated_from"),
    55	        )

    58	@dataclass
    59	class AuditResult:
    60	    """Result of an audit logging operation."""
    61	
    62	    success: bool
    63	    entry_id: str | None = None
    64	    error: str | None = None
    65	
    66	    @classmethod
    67	    def from_dict(cls, data: dict[str, Any]) -> "AuditResult":
    68	        return cls(
    69	            success=data.get("success", False),
    70	            entry_id=data.get("entry_id") or data.get("id"),
    71	            error=data.get("error"),
    72	        )

    74	
    75	class AuditService:
    76	    """Service for audit trail logging and querying."""
    77	
    78	    def __init__(self, db: DatabaseClient | None = None):
    79	        self._db = db
    80	        #: Strong references to in-flight fire-and-forget insert tasks.
    81	        #:
    82	        #: ``asyncio`` keeps only a *weak* reference to a task, so a bare
    83	        #: ``create_task(...)`` whose result nobody holds may be garbage
    84	        #: collected before it runs. Holding the task until it completes is the
    85	        #: documented way to make fire-and-forget actually fire.
    86	        self._pending: set[asyncio.Task[AuditResult]] = set()
    87	
    88	    @property
    89	    def db(self) -> DatabaseClient:
    90	        if self._db is None:
    91	            self._db = get_db()
    92	        return self._db
    93	
    94	    async def log_operation(
    95	        self,
    96	        agent_id: str | None = None,
    97	        agent_type: str | None = None,
    98	        operation: str = "",
    99	        parameters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   100	        result: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
   101	        duration_ms: int | None = None,
   102	        success: bool | None = None,
   103	        error_message: str | None = None,
   104	        delegated_from: str | None = None,
   105	        session_id: str | None = None,
   106	    ) -> AuditResult:
   107	        """Log a coordination operation to the audit trail.
   108	
   109	        When async_logging is enabled (default), this fires-and-forgets
   110	        the insert to avoid blocking the caller.
   111	
   112	        Also pushes the entry into the audit-triage ring buffer (D9)
   113	        for downstream LLM classification.  The push is synchronous
   114	        and microsecond-fast — no LLM involvement on the hot path.
   115	        """
   116	        config = get_config()
   117	        agent_id = agent_id or config.agent.agent_id
   118	        agent_type = agent_type or config.agent.agent_type
   119	
   120	        data = {
   121	            "agent_id": agent_id,
   122	            "agent_type": agent_type,
   123	            "operation": operation,
   124	            "parameters": parameters or {},
   125	            "result": result or {},
   126	            "duration_ms": duration_ms,
   127	            "success": success,
   128	            "error_message": error_message,
   129	            "delegated_from": delegated_from,
   130	        }
   131	
   132	        # Push to audit-triage ring buffer (D9: hot path, no LLM)
   133	        try:
   134	            from .audit_triage import get_triage_buffer
   135	
   136	            entry = AuditEntry(
   137	                id="",
   138	                agent_id=agent_id,
   139	                agent_type=agent_type,
   140	                operation=operation,
   141	                parameters=parameters or {},
   142	                result=result or {},
   143	                duration_ms=duration_ms,
   144	                success=success,
   145	                error_message=error_message,
   146	                delegated_from=delegated_from,
   147	            )
   148	            resolved_session_id = session_id or (config.agent.session_id or "unknown")
   149	            get_triage_buffer().push(entry, session_id=resolved_session_id)
   150	        except Exception:
   151	            # Never let triage buffer failures affect the audit hot path
   152	            pass
   153	
   154	        if config.audit.async_logging:
   155	            # Fire-and-forget: don't block the caller. `success=True` here means
   156	            # "accepted for writing", not "written" — the insert has not run yet.
   157	            task = asyncio.create_task(self._insert_audit_entry(data))
   158	            self._pending.add(task)
   159	            task.add_done_callback(self._pending.discard)
   160	            return AuditResult(success=True)
   161	        else:
   162	            return await self._insert_audit_entry(data)
   163	
   164	    async def drain(self, timeout: float = 5.0) -> None:
   165	        """Wait for in-flight fire-and-forget audit inserts to finish.
   166	
   167	        Callers that need the trail to exist before they continue — startup
   168	        projections, shutdown, and tests — await this. Without it a short-lived
   169	        process can exit before the loop ever runs the queued inserts, which is
   170	        indistinguishable from the writes failing.
   171	
   172	        Raises:
   173	            TimeoutError: if ``timeout`` elapses while inserts are still
   174	                outstanding. ``asyncio.wait`` returns a ``(done, pending)``
   175	                pair rather than raising on timeout, so a caller that ignores
   176	                it would see ``drain()`` return normally and believe the
   177	                audit trail is durable when it is not — the same
   178	                returned-but-unread failure mode ``_insert_audit_entry``
   179	                documents, one layer up. Raising makes the timeout
   180	                impossible to silently ignore.
   181	        """
   182	        if not self._pending:
   183	            return
   184	        done, pending = await asyncio.wait(set(self._pending), timeout=timeout)
   185	        if pending:
   186	            logger.error(
   187	                "Audit drain timed out after %.1fs with %d insert(s) still "
   188	                "outstanding — the audit trail is not guaranteed durable.",
   189	                timeout,
   190	                len(pending),
   191	            )
   192	            raise TimeoutError(
   193	                f"AuditService.drain() timed out after {timeout}s with "
   194	                f"{len(pending)} audit insert(s) still outstanding"
   195	            )
   196	
   197	    async def _insert_audit_entry(self, data: dict[str, Any]) -> AuditResult:
   198	        """Insert an audit entry into the database.
   199	
   200	        Failures are logged rather than only returned. On the fire-and-forget
   201	        path nobody awaits the result, so a returned-but-unread error is the
   202	        same as no error at all — which is exactly how the audit trail came to
   203	        record nothing at all on the PostgreSQL backend for every operation:
   204	        ``log_operation`` built a payload containing ``delegated_from``, a
   205	        column ``audit_log`` did not have until migration 035, so every insert
   206	        raised, the exception was swallowed here, the failed result was
   207	        discarded by the caller, and callers were told ``success=True``.
   208	        """
   209	        try:
   210	            row = await self.db.insert("audit_log", data)
   211	            return AuditResult(success=True, entry_id=str(row.get("id", "")))
   212	        except Exception as e:
   213	            logger.error(
   214	                "Audit write failed for operation %r — the audit trail is "
   215	                "incomplete: %s",
   216	                data.get("operation"),
   217	                e,
   218	                exc_info=True,
   219	            )
   220	            return AuditResult(success=False, error=str(e))
   221	
   222	    async def query(
   223	        self,
   224	        agent_id: str | None = None,
   225	        operation: str | None = None,
   226	        since: datetime | None = None,
   227	        until: datetime | None = None,
   228	        limit: int = 50,
   229	        delegated_from: str | None = None,
   230	        change_id: str | None = None,
   231	    ) -> list[AuditEntry]:
   232	        """Query audit log entries with optional filters.
   233	
   234	        New filters (additive, backward-compatible; all optional):
   235	        - ``since``: ISO-8601 timestamp; returns entries with
   236	          ``created_at >= since``.
   237	        - ``change_id``: filters entries whose ``parameters`` JSONB column
   238	          contains ``{"change_id": "<id>"}`` (recorded by most call-sites)
   239	          OR whose ``agent_id`` maps to an ``agent_sessions.change_id``
   240	          match (fallback, best-effort).
   241	        """
   242	        query_parts = ["order=created_at.desc", f"limit={limit}"]
   243	
   244	        if agent_id:
   245	            query_parts.append(f"agent_id=eq.{agent_id}")
   246	        if operation:
   247	            query_parts.append(f"operation=eq.{operation}")
   248	        if since:
   249	            query_parts.append(f"created_at=gte.{since.isoformat()}")
   250	        if until:
   251	            query_parts.append(f"created_at=lte.{until.isoformat()}")
   252	        if delegated_from:
   253	            query_parts.append(f"delegated_from=eq.{delegated_from}")
   254	        if change_id:
   255	            # Filter on parameters JSONB containing change_id key.
   256	            # PostgREST/Supabase: parameters->>change_id=eq.<value>
   257	            # PostgresClient: appended as a raw query param string.
   258	            query_parts.append(f"parameters->>change_id=eq.{change_id}")
   259	
   260	        query = "&".join(query_parts)
   261	        rows = await self.db.query("audit_log", query)
   262	        return [AuditEntry.from_dict(row) for row in rows]
   263	
   264	    def timed(self, operation: str) -> "AuditTimer":
   265	        """Create a context manager for timing and logging an operation."""
   266	        return AuditTimer(self, operation)
   267	
   268	
   269	class AuditTimer:
   270	    """Context manager for timing operations and logging to audit trail."""
   271	
   272	    def __init__(self, service: AuditService, operation: str):
   273	        self.service = service
   274	        self.operation = operation
   275	        self._start: float = 0
   276	
   277	    async def __aenter__(self) -> "AuditTimer":
   278	        self._start = time.monotonic()
   279	        return self
   280	
   281	    async def __aexit__(
   282	        self,
   283	        exc_type: type[BaseException] | None,
   284	        exc_val: BaseException | None,
   285	        exc_tb: Any,
   286	    ) -> None:
   287	        duration_ms = int((time.monotonic() - self._start) * 1000)
   288	        await self.service.log_operation(
   289	            operation=self.operation,
   290	            duration_ms=duration_ms,
   291	            success=exc_type is None,
   292	            error_message=str(exc_val) if exc_val else None,
   293	        )
   294

   296	# Global service instance
   297	_audit_service: AuditService | None = None
   298	
   299	
   300	def get_audit_service() -> AuditService:
   301	    """Get the global audit service instance."""
   302	    global _audit_service
   303	    if _audit_service is None:
   304	        _audit_service = AuditService()
   305	    return _audit_service

   744	
   745	    Structured on purpose (``rule`` / ``tier`` / ``detail``): an unattended

   757	            if tier

  1186	def derive_allowed_operations(
  1187	    capabilities: list[str] | tuple[str, ...],
  1188	    trust_level: int,
  1189	) -> list[str]:
  1190	    """Project a registry entry's capabilities + trust level to operations.
  1191	
  1192	    Two dimensions, because the hand-written migrations used two: capabilities
  1193	    map to the operation families they name, and trust level independently
  1194	    grants the merge-queue operations no capability covers (migration 022).
  1195	
  1196	    Raises:
  1197	        ValueError: If a capability has no mapping — a half-onboarded harness
  1198	            must fail loudly rather than materialize a profile missing grants.
  1199	    """
  1200	    operations: set[str] = set(UNIVERSAL_OPERATIONS)
  1201	    for capability in capabilities:
  1202	        mapped = CAPABILITY_OPERATIONS.get(capability)
  1203	        if mapped is None:
  1204	            raise ValueError(
  1205	                f"Capability '{capability}' has no operation mapping; add it to "
  1206	                f"CAPABILITY_OPERATIONS. Known capabilities: "
  1207	                f"{sorted(CAPABILITY_OPERATIONS)}"
  1208	            )
  1209	        operations.update(mapped)
  1210	
  1211	    for minimum_trust, granted in TRUST_DERIVED_OPERATIONS:
  1212	        if trust_level >= minimum_trust:
  1213	            operations.update(granted)
  1214	
  1215	    return sorted(operations)
  1216	
  1217	
  1218	#: Substring PostgreSQL puts in the message of every UNIQUE-constraint failure.
  1219	#: The PostgREST/httpx backend surfaces the violation as text, so the string is
  1220	#: the only signal available there.
  1221	_UNIQUE_VIOLATION_TEXT = "duplicate key value violates unique constraint"
  1222	
  1223	#: SQLSTATE for unique_violation. asyncpg exposes it as ``sqlstate``.
  1224	_UNIQUE_VIOLATION_SQLSTATE = "23505"
  1225	
  1226	
  1227	def _is_unique_violation(exc: BaseException) -> bool:
  1228	    """Is *exc* a genuine UNIQUE-constraint violation?
  1229	
  1230	    The insert→update fallbacks below exist for exactly one situation: a
  1231	    concurrent worker won the race for the same unique key. Treating *every*
  1232	    insert failure as that race is what let an RLS denial, an FK violation, or
  1233	    a CHECK failure be retried as an UPDATE — which matches zero rows, raises
  1234	    nothing (``return_data=False`` never inspects rowcount), and is then
  1235	    recorded as a successful projection with an audit event for a row that
  1236	    does not exist. Anything that is not a uniqueness collision must fail the
  1237	    sync instead.
  1238	    """
  1239	    if type(exc).__name__ == "UniqueViolationError":  # asyncpg
  1240	        return True
  1241	    if getattr(exc, "sqlstate", None) == _UNIQUE_VIOLATION_SQLSTATE:
  1242	        return True
  1243	    return _UNIQUE_VIOLATION_TEXT in str(exc)
  1244	
  1245	
  1246	def _registry_sync_timestamp() -> datetime:
  1247	    """Value for ``agent_profiles.synced_from_registry_at`` on this write.
  1248	
  1249	    Migration 032 added the column so operators can tell registry-projected
  1250	    rows from hand-maintained ones; it stays NULL unless the projection
  1251	    actually stamps it.
  1252	
  1253	    Returns a ``datetime``, never an ISO string: asyncpg binds TIMESTAMPTZ
  1254	    parameters from datetime objects only, and a str here fails every boot
  1255	    whose sync needs a profile write (DataError at bind time) — which the
  1256	    mocked-DB tests cannot see because ``FakeDb`` accepts any payload. This
  1257	    took production down on 2026-08-22; the type is load-bearing.
  1258	    """
  1259	    return datetime.now(UTC)

  1263	    """Build the ``agent_profiles`` row a registry entry projects to."""

  1274	
  1275	def _profile_drift(
  1276	    desired: dict[str, Any],
  1277	    existing: dict[str, Any],
  1278	) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
  1279	    """Return ``{field: {"from": old, "to": new}}`` for drifted tracked fields."""
  1280	    changed: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
  1281	    for name in SYNC_TRACKED_FIELDS:
  1282	        current = existing.get(name)
  1283	        target = desired[name]
  1284	        if name == "allowed_operations":
  1285	            current = sorted(current or [])
  1286	        if name == "enabled":
  1287	            current = bool(current)
  1288	        if current != target:
  1289	            changed[name] = {"from": current, "to": target}
  1290	    return changed

  1293	async def _emit_sync_audit(
  1294	    audit: AuditService,
  1295	    *,
  1296	    action: str,
  1297	    profile_name: str,
  1298	    agent_type: str,
  1299	    trust_level: int | None = None,
  1300	    changed_fields: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
  1301	    agent_id: str | None = None,
  1302	    previous_profile_name: str | None = None,
  1303	) -> None:
  1304	    """Emit one profile-sync audit event (contract: profile-sync-audit.schema.json)."""
  1305	    parameters: dict[str, Any] = {
  1306	        "action": action,
  1307	        "profile_name": profile_name,
  1308	        "agent_type": agent_type,
  1309	        "source": PROFILE_SYNC_SOURCE,
  1310	    }
  1311	    if trust_level is not None:
  1312	        parameters["trust_level"] = trust_level
  1313	    if changed_fields:
  1314	        parameters["changed_fields"] = changed_fields
  1315	    if agent_id is not None:
  1316	        parameters["agent_id"] = agent_id
  1317	    if previous_profile_name is not None:
  1318	        parameters["previous_profile_name"] = previous_profile_name
  1319	
  1320	    try:
  1321	        await audit.log_operation(
  1322	            operation=PROFILE_SYNC_OPERATION,
  1323	            parameters=parameters,
  1324	            result={"profile_name": profile_name},
  1325	            success=True,
  1326	        )
  1327	    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
  1328	        # The projection itself succeeded; losing its audit event degrades
  1329	        # observability but must not roll back or block boot.
  1330	        logger.warning(
  1331	            "Failed to audit profile_sync %s for profile '%s'",
  1332	            action,
  1333	            profile_name,
  1334	            exc_info=True,
  1335	        )

  1337	
  1338	async def _sync_assignments(
  1339	    agents: list[AgentEntry],
  1340	    *,
  1341	    db: DatabaseClient,
  1342	    audit: AuditService,
  1343	    result: ProfileSyncResult,
  1344	) -> None:
  1345	    """Project ``agent_profile_assignments`` from the registry (design D11).
  1346	
  1347	    Profiles alone do not decide what an agent resolves to.
  1348	    ``get_agent_profile()`` (migration 007) reads the assignment first and only
  1349	    then falls back to ``agent_type`` + ``ORDER BY created_at ASC LIMIT 1``.
  1350	    That fallback silently serves the *oldest* row of the type when two agents
  1351	    share a type and neither is assigned — the bug migration 018 fixed by hand
  1352	    for the roster of its day and for nobody added since. Writing one assignment
  1353	    per registry agent makes the tiebreak unreachable rather than merely lucky.
  1354	
  1355	    Idempotent and convergent under concurrent worker boot, like the profile
  1356	    phase: writes are keyed on ``agent_id`` (the table's UNIQUE column), so a
  1357	    worker that loses the INSERT race reconciles with an UPDATE.
  1358	    """
  1359	    # Profile ids are not returned by the upsert path above, so re-query. This
  1360	    # also picks up rows a concurrent worker inserted between our phases.
  1740	        "assignments: %d assigned, %d reassigned, %d removed, %d unchanged.",
  1741	        len(result.inserted),
  1742	        len(result.updated),
  1743	        len(result.disabled),
  1744	        len(result.unchanged),
  1745	        len(result.assigned),
  1746	        len(result.reassigned),
  1747	        len(result.unassigned),
  1748	        len(result.assignments_unchanged),
  1749	    )
  1750	    return result

  1757	def get_mcp_env(
  1758	    agent_id: str,
  1759	    agents: list[AgentEntry] | None = None,
  1760	) -> dict[str, str]:
  1761	    """Generate env vars for MCP server registration of *agent_id*.
  1762	
  1763	    Returns:
  1764	        Dict of environment variables (``AGENT_ID``, ``AGENT_TYPE``, and
  1765	        database settings from the current environment).
  1766	    """
  1767	    if agents is None:
  1768	        agents = load_agents_config()
  1769	
  1770	    agent = next((a for a in agents if a.name == agent_id), None)
  1771	    if agent is None:
  1772	        raise ValueError(f"Agent '{agent_id}' not found in agents.yaml")
  1773	
  1774	    env: dict[str, str] = {
  1775	        "AGENT_ID": agent.name,
  1776	        "AGENT_TYPE": agent.type,
  1777	    }
  1778	
  1779	    # Include database connection settings from the current environment.
  1780	    for key in ("DB_BACKEND", "POSTGRES_DSN", "POSTGRES_POOL_MIN", "POSTGRES_POOL_MAX"):
  1781	        val = os.environ.get(key)
  1782	        if val:
  1783	            env[key] = val
  1784	
  1785	    return env

  1828	
  1829	def get_dispatch_configs(
  1830	    agents: list[AgentEntry] | None = None,
  1831	) -> dict[str, Any]:
  1832	    """Return configs for agents with a dispatch transport or routable endpoint.
  1833	
  1834	    Shared serialization logic used by both MCP and HTTP endpoints.
  1835	    Returns a dict with ``agents`` key containing a list of agent
  1836	    dispatch config dicts.
  1837	    """
  1838	    if agents is None:
  1839	        agents = get_agents_config()
  1840	
  1841	    agents_out: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
  1842	    for entry in agents:
  1843	        routable_endpoint = (
  1844	            entry.endpoint_kind in {"openrouter", "local"} and entry.base_url
  1845	        )
  1846	        if entry.cli is None and entry.sdk is None and not routable_endpoint:
  1847	            continue
  1848	        sdk_out: dict[str, Any] | None = None
  1849	        if entry.sdk:
  1850	            sdk_out = {
  1851	                "package": entry.sdk.package,
  1852	                "model": entry.sdk.model,
  1853	                "method": entry.sdk.method,
  1854	                "model_fallbacks": entry.sdk.model_fallbacks,
  1855	                "api_key_env": entry.sdk.api_key_env,
  1856	                "max_tokens": entry.sdk.max_tokens,
  1857	            }
  1858	        cli_out: dict[str, Any] | None = None
  1859	        if entry.cli:
  1860	            cli_out = {
  1861	                "command": entry.cli.command,
  1862	                "dispatch_modes": {
  1863	                    name: {
  1864	                        "args": mc.args,
  1865	                        "async": mc.async_dispatch,
  1866	                        **(
  1867	                            {"isolation": mc.isolation}
  1868	                            if mc.isolation is not None
  1869	                            else {}
  1870	                        ),
  1871	                        **({"poll": {
  1872	                            "command_template": mc.poll.command_template,
  1873	                            "result_protocol": mc.poll.result_protocol,
  1874	                            "interval_seconds": mc.poll.interval_seconds,
  1875	                            "timeout_seconds": mc.poll.timeout_seconds,
  1876	                        }} if mc.poll else {}),
  1877	                    }
  1878	                    for name, mc in entry.cli.dispatch_modes.items()
  1879	                },
  1880	                "model_flag": entry.cli.model_flag,
  1881	                "model": entry.cli.model,
  1882	                "model_fallbacks": entry.cli.model_fallbacks,
  1883	                "prompt_via_stdin": entry.cli.prompt_via_stdin,
  1884	                "prompt_via_flag": entry.cli.prompt_via_flag,
  1885	                "api_key_env": entry.cli.api_key_env,
  1886	            }
  1887	        agents_out.append({
  1888	            "agent_id": entry.name,
  1889	            "type": entry.type,
  1890	            "transport": entry.transport,
  1891	            "openbao_role_id": entry.openbao_role_id,
  1892	            "endpoint_kind": entry.endpoint_kind,
  1893	            "base_url": entry.base_url,
  1894	            "cli": cli_out,
  1895	            "sdk": sdk_out,
  1896	        })
  1897	
  1898	    return {"agents": agents_out}

  1901	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1902	# Isolation helpers
  1903	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1904	
  1905	def get_agent_isolation(
  1906	    agent_type: str,
  1907	    dispatch_mode: str | None = None,
  1908	    *,
  1909	    agent_id: str | None = None,
  1910	) -> IsolationMode | None:
  1911	    """Return isolation for an exact agent/mode, or ``None`` if not found.
  1912	
  1913	    The legacy one-argument call retains first-type-match behavior. Callers
  1914	    that know the selected lane pass ``agent_id`` to avoid YAML-order coupling.
  1915	    """
  1916	    for agent in get_agents_config():
  1917	        if agent.type != agent_type or (agent_id is not None and agent.name != agent_id):
  1918	            continue
  1919	        configured: object = agent.isolation
  1920	        if dispatch_mode is not None and agent.cli is not None:
  1921	            mode = agent.cli.dispatch_modes.get(dispatch_mode)
  1922	            if mode is not None and mode.isolation is not None:
  1923	                configured = mode.isolation
  1924	        return validate_isolation(configured, rung="agents_yaml")
  1925	    return None

  2470	
  2471	def resolve_model(
  2472	    archetype: ArchetypeConfig,
  2473	    package_metadata: dict[str, Any],
  2474	    *,
  2475	    return_reasons: bool = False,
  2476	    phase: str | None = None,
  2477	    provider: str | None = None,
  2478	    model_map: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
  2479	) -> str | tuple[str, list[str]]:
  2480	    """Resolve the effective model for a work package.
  2481	
  2482	    Checks escalation rules from the archetype config against package
  2483	    metadata.  All thresholds come from ``archetypes.yaml`` — no
  2484	    hardcoded values (design decision D1).
  2485	
  2486	    Args:
  2487	        archetype: The archetype configuration.
  2488	        package_metadata: Dict with optional keys: ``write_allow``,
  2489	            ``dependencies``, ``loc_estimate``, ``complexity``.
  2490	        return_reasons: If True, return a tuple of (model, reasons).
  2491	        phase: Optional autopilot phase name. Currently used only to enrich
  2492	            log messages (design decision D3); does not change escalation
  2493	            behavior. Reserved for future phase-specific escalation rules.
  2494	        provider: Optional provider id. When supplied, the logical or legacy
  2495	            archetype model resolves to a provider-specific model ID.
  2496	
  2497	    Returns:
  2498	        The resolved model string, or (model, reasons) if *return_reasons*.
  2499	    """
  2500	    spec, reasons = _resolve_model_spec(
  2501	        archetype,
  2502	        package_metadata,
  2503	        phase=phase,
  2504	        provider=provider,
  2505	        model_map=model_map,
  2506	    )
  2507	    return (spec.model, reasons) if return_reasons else spec.model
  2508	
  2509	
  2510	def _resolve_model_spec(
  2511	    archetype: ArchetypeConfig,
  2512	    package_metadata: dict[str, Any],
  2513	    *,
  2514	    phase: str | None = None,
  2515	    provider: str | None = None,
  2516	    model_map: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
  2517	) -> tuple[ModelSpec, list[str]]:
  2518	    """Escalation pipeline returning the full ModelSpec (model + thinking)."""
  2519	    def _finalize(source_model: str, reasons: list[str]) -> tuple[ModelSpec, list[str]]:
  2520	        degradation: list[str] = []
  2521	        spec = resolve_provider_model_spec(
  2522	            source_model,
  2523	            provider=provider,
  2524	            model_map=model_map,
  2525	            reasons=degradation,
  2526	        )
  2527	        if degradation:
  2528	            reasons = [*reasons, *degradation]
  2529	        if provider and spec.model != source_model:
  2530	            suffix = f" (thinking={spec.thinking})" if spec.thinking else ""
  2531	            reasons = [
  2532	                *reasons,
  2533	                f"provider={provider} mapped {source_model} to {spec.model}{suffix}",
  2534	            ]
  2535	        return spec, reasons
  2536	
  2537	    if not archetype.escalation:
  2538	        return _finalize(archetype.model, [])
  2539	
  2540	    rules = archetype.escalation
  2541	    reasons: list[str] = []
  2542	
  2543	    write_allow = package_metadata.get("write_allow", [])
  2544	    if rules.max_write_dirs and _unique_dir_prefixes(write_allow) > rules.max_write_dirs:
  2545	        reasons.append(f"write_allow spans >{rules.max_write_dirs} directories")
  2546	
  2547	    dependencies = package_metadata.get("dependencies", [])
  2548	    if rules.max_dependencies and len(dependencies) > rules.max_dependencies:
  2549	        reasons.append(f"depends on >{rules.max_dependencies} packages")
  2550	
  2551	    loc_estimate = package_metadata.get("loc_estimate", 0) or 0
  2552	    if rules.loc_threshold and loc_estimate > rules.loc_threshold:
  2553	        reasons.append(f"loc_estimate >{rules.loc_threshold}")
  2554	
  2555	    if package_metadata.get("complexity") == "high":
  2556	        reasons.append("explicit complexity: high flag")
  2557	
  2558	    if reasons:
  2559	        escalated_model = rules.escalate_to
  2560	        if phase:
  2561	            logger.info(
  2562	                "Escalating %s to %s for phase %s: %s",
  2563	                archetype.name, escalated_model, phase, ", ".join(reasons),
  2564	            )
  2565	        else:
  2566	            logger.info(
  2567	                "Escalating %s to %s: %s",
  2568	                archetype.name, escalated_model, ", ".join(reasons),
  2569	            )
  2570	        return _finalize(escalated_model, reasons)
  2571	
  2572	    return _finalize(archetype.model, [])
  2573	
  2574	
  2575	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2576	# Phase-aware archetype resolution (D2: coordinator-owned phase mapping)
  2577	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2578	
  2579	
  2580	def _resolve_archetype_for_phase_static(
  2581	    phase: str,
  2582	    signals: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
  2583	    *,
  2584	    provider: str | None = None,
  2585	) -> ResolvedArchetype:
  2586	    """Resolve archetype, model, and system_prompt for an autopilot phase.
  2587	
  2588	    Looks up *phase* in the ``phase_mapping`` section of ``archetypes.yaml``,
  2589	    resolves the configured archetype, and runs the standard escalation
  2590	    pipeline against *signals* (filtered to the keys listed in the phase
  2591	    entry's ``signals`` field — unknown keys are silently dropped).
  2592	
  2593	    Args:
  2594	        phase: One of the 13 non-terminal autopilot phase names.
  2595	        signals: Free-form signal dict from the caller; only keys listed in
  2596	            the phase entry's ``signals`` are used for escalation.
  2597	
  2598	    Returns:
  2599	        A :class:`ResolvedArchetype` carrying the model, system prompt,
  2600	        archetype name, procedure mode, and a reasons trace. For a non-guided
  2601	        ``procedure_mode`` the archetype's ``system_prompt`` is returned with
  2602	        the mode's sentence from :data:`PROCEDURE_MODE_SENTENCES` appended
  2603	        after one blank line (add-skill-audit D3). This is the only injection
  2604	        point; ``guided`` returns the prompt unchanged.
  2605	
  2606	    Raises:
  2607	        KeyError: If *phase* is not present in ``phase_mapping``.
  2608	        RuntimeError: If the cached archetypes config has been mutated such
  2609	            that the phase entry's archetype reference is no longer valid.
  2610	        LocalProviderTrustBoundaryError: If *provider* is ``local`` and the
  2611	            phase's archetype is outside :data:`LOCAL_TRUSTED_ARCHETYPES`
  2612	            (design D3) — raised before any model resolution or dispatch.
  2613	    """
  2614	    if _phase_mapping is None:
  2615	        load_archetypes_config()
  2616	    mapping = _phase_mapping if _phase_mapping is not None else {}
  2617	
  2618	    if phase not in mapping:
  2619	        raise KeyError(
  2620	            f"Phase {phase!r} not found in phase_mapping; "
  2621	            f"defined phases: {sorted(mapping.keys()) or 'none'}"
  2622	        )
  2623	
  2624	    entry = mapping[phase]
  2625	    archetype = get_archetype(entry.archetype)
  2626	    if archetype is None:
  2627	        # Validated at load time; this branch only fires if the cache is mutated.
  2628	        raise RuntimeError(
  2629	            f"phase_mapping[{phase!r}] references undefined archetype "
  2630	            f"{entry.archetype!r} (cache may be stale; call "
  2631	            f"reset_archetypes_config() and reload)"
  2632	        )
  2633	
  2634	    # Enforce the `local` provider trust boundary (design D3) before anything
  2635	    # is resolved or dispatched: local models are permitted only where their
  2636	    # output is cheap to discard or verified downstream. The coordinator is the
  2637	    # single decision point, so no client can route around this check.
  2638	    boundary_reasons: list[str] = []
  2639	    if provider == LOCAL_PROVIDER:
  2640	        if archetype.name not in LOCAL_TRUSTED_ARCHETYPES:
  2641	            raise LocalProviderTrustBoundaryError(archetype.name, phase=phase)
  2642	        boundary_reasons.append(
  2643	            f"provider={LOCAL_PROVIDER} trust boundary checked: archetype="
  2644	            f"{archetype.name} is permitted "
  2645	            f"({', '.join(sorted(LOCAL_TRUSTED_ARCHETYPES))})"
  2646	        )
  2647	
  2648	    # Enforce the write-capability contract at resolution time (design D3 /
  2649	    # Task 2.5): a write-capable phase MUST resolve to a write_capable archetype.
  2650	    # This is the structured-field gate — no substring matching over prompts.
  2651	    if phase in WRITE_CAPABLE_PHASES and not archetype.write_capable:
  2652	        raise ValueError(
  2653	            f"phase_mapping[{phase!r}] resolves to archetype "
  2654	            f"{archetype.name!r} with write_capable=false, but {phase} is a "
  2655	            f"write-capable phase that produces files/artifacts/handoffs. "
  2656	            f"Map it to an archetype with write_capable: true in archetypes.yaml."
  2657	        )
  2658	
  2659	    # Filter signals to keys listed in the phase entry — security-style
  2660	    # whitelist that mirrors the spec's "unknown keys silently dropped" rule.
  2661	    filtered: dict[str, Any] = {

    53	ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING;
    54	
    55	-- =============================================================================
    56	-- Functions
    57	-- =============================================================================
    58	
    59	CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION is_domain_allowed(
    60	    p_agent_id TEXT,
    61	    p_domain TEXT
    62	)
    63	RETURNS JSONB
    64	LANGUAGE plpgsql
    65	AS $$
    66	DECLARE
    67	    v_profile_id UUID;
    68	    v_policy RECORD;
    69	    v_allowed BOOLEAN := false;
    70	    v_reason TEXT := 'no_matching_policy';
    71	    v_policy_id UUID;
    72	BEGIN
    73	    -- Get agent's profile ID
    74	    SELECT pa.profile_id INTO v_profile_id
    75	    FROM agent_profile_assignments pa
    76	    WHERE pa.agent_id = p_agent_id;
    77	
    78	    -- Check policies: profile-specific first, then global (NULL profile_id)
    79	    -- Higher priority (lower number) wins
    80	    FOR v_policy IN
    81	        SELECT np.*
    82	        FROM network_policies np
    83	        WHERE np.enabled = true
    84	          AND (np.profile_id = v_profile_id OR np.profile_id IS NULL)
    85	          AND (
    86	              p_domain = np.domain_pattern
    87	              OR p_domain LIKE REPLACE(np.domain_pattern, '*', '%')
    88	          )
    89	        ORDER BY
    90	            CASE WHEN np.profile_id IS NOT NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END,  -- profile-specific first
    91	            np.priority ASC
    92	        LIMIT 1
    93	    LOOP
    94	        v_allowed := (v_policy.action = 'allow');
    95	        v_reason := v_policy.action;
    96	        v_policy_id := v_policy.id;
    97	    END LOOP;
    98	
    99	    -- Log the access attempt
   100	    INSERT INTO network_access_log (agent_id, domain, allowed, policy_id, reason)
   101	    VALUES (p_agent_id, p_domain, v_allowed, v_policy_id, v_reason);
   102	
   103	    RETURN jsonb_build_object(
   104	        'allowed', v_allowed,
   105	        'domain', p_domain,
   106	        'reason', v_reason,
   107	        'policy_id', v_policy_id
   108	    );
   109	END;
   110	$$;
   111	
   112	-- =============================================================================
   113	-- Row Level Security
   114	-- =============================================================================
   115

   117	ALTER TABLE network_access_log ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

   508	
   509	def classify_error(text: str) -> ErrorClass:
   510	    """Classify a vendor error from its output text.
   511	
   512	    Accepts stderr OR stdout — some CLIs (pi) exit 0 with the provider's
   513	    error body on stdout (issue #383), so classification cannot assume the
   514	    text arrived on stderr. UNAVAILABLE is checked first: a billing body
   515	    ("Insufficient credits … upgrade your limit") contains words that would
   516	    otherwise false-positive the capacity patterns.
   517	    """
   518	    lower = text.lower()
   519	    if any(p in lower for p in _UNAVAILABLE_PATTERNS) or _UNAVAILABLE_402_RE.search(lower):
   520	        return ErrorClass.UNAVAILABLE
   521	    if any(p in lower for p in _AUTH_PATTERNS):
   522	        return ErrorClass.AUTH
   523	    if any(p in lower for p in _CAPACITY_PATTERNS):
   524	        return ErrorClass.CAPACITY
   525	    if any(p in lower for p in _TRANSIENT_PATTERNS):
   526	        return ErrorClass.TRANSIENT
   527	    return ErrorClass.UNKNOWN

   602	class VendorResultProtocolError(ValueError):
   603	    """Raised when a vendor does not emit the contracted result envelope."""
   604	
   605	
   606	@dataclass(frozen=True)
   607	class VendorResultEnvelope:
   608	    """Versioned, normalized vendor result returned by CLI adapter commands."""
   609	
   610	    version: int
   611	    state: str
   612	    vendor_task_id: str | None = None
   613	    result: dict[str, Any] | None = None
   614	    error: dict[str, Any] | None = None
   615	
   616	    @property
   617	    def is_terminal(self) -> bool:
   618	        return self.state in {"succeeded", "failed", "cancelled"}
   619	
   620	    def as_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
   621	        """Return the stable JSON representation persisted in the ledger."""
   622	        return {
   623	            "version": self.version,
   624	            "state": self.state,
   625	            "vendor_task_id": self.vendor_task_id,
   626	            "result": self.result,
   627	            "error": self.error,
   628	        }
   629	
   630	
   631	def parse_vendor_result_envelope(payload: str) -> VendorResultEnvelope:
   632	    """Parse one CLI result without a legacy stdout-regex fallback."""
   633	    try:
   634	        data = json.loads(payload)
   635	    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
   636	        raise VendorResultProtocolError("invalid JSON vendor result envelope") from exc
   637	    if not isinstance(data, dict):
   638	        raise VendorResultProtocolError("vendor result envelope must be an object")
   639	    allowed_fields = {"version", "state", "vendor_task_id", "result", "error"}
   640	    unexpected_fields = sorted(set(data) - allowed_fields)
   641	    if unexpected_fields:
   642	        raise VendorResultProtocolError(
   643	            f"vendor result envelope has unexpected field: {unexpected_fields[0]}"
   644	        )
   645	    version = data.get("version")
   646	    if isinstance(version, bool) or not isinstance(version, int) or version != 1:
   647	        raise VendorResultProtocolError("unsupported vendor result envelope version")
   648	    state = data.get("state")
   649	    valid_states = {"submitted", "running", "succeeded", "failed", "cancelled"}
   650	    if state not in valid_states:
   651	        raise VendorResultProtocolError("vendor result envelope has invalid state")
   652	    vendor_task_id = data.get("vendor_task_id")
   653	    if vendor_task_id is not None and not isinstance(vendor_task_id, str):
   654	        raise VendorResultProtocolError("vendor_task_id must be a string or null")
   655	    if vendor_task_id == "":
   656	        raise VendorResultProtocolError("vendor_task_id must not be empty")
   657	    if state in {"submitted", "running"} and not vendor_task_id:
   658	        raise VendorResultProtocolError(
   659	            "nonterminal vendor result envelope requires vendor_task_id"
   660	        )
   661	    result = data.get("result")
   662	    error = data.get("error")
   663	    if result is not None and not isinstance(result, dict):
   664	        raise VendorResultProtocolError("vendor result envelope result must be an object")
   665	    if error is not None and not isinstance(error, dict):
   666	        raise VendorResultProtocolError("vendor result envelope error must be an object")
   667	    if state == "succeeded" and result is None:
   668	        raise VendorResultProtocolError(
   669	            "succeeded vendor result envelope requires result"
   670	        )
   671	    if state in {"failed", "cancelled"} and error is None:
   672	        raise VendorResultProtocolError(
   673	            f"{state} vendor result envelope requires error"
   674	        )
   675	    if isinstance(error, dict):
   676	        message = error.get("message")
   677	        if not isinstance(message, str):
   678	            raise VendorResultProtocolError(
   679	                "vendor result envelope error requires a message"
   680	            )
   681	        if not message:
   682	            raise VendorResultProtocolError("error message must not be empty")
   683	        error_code = error.get("code")
   684	        if error_code is not None and (not isinstance(error_code, str) or not error_code):
   685	            raise VendorResultProtocolError("error code must be a non-empty string")
   686	    return VendorResultEnvelope(
   687	        version=1,
   688	        state=state,
   689	        vendor_task_id=vendor_task_id,
   690	        result=result,
   691	        error=error,
   692	    )

   695	@dataclass
   696	class ReviewResult:
   697	    """Result from a vendor review dispatch."""
   698	
   699	    vendor: str
   700	    success: bool
   701	    findings: dict[str, Any] | None = None
   702	    model_used: str | None = None
   703	    models_attempted: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
   704	    elapsed_seconds: float = 0.0
   705	    error: str | None = None
   706	    error_class: ErrorClass | None = None
   707	    async_dispatch: bool = False
   708	    task_id: str | None = None
   709	    ledger_task_id: str | None = None
   710	    # OpenRouter/OpenAI-compatible generation id for spend reconciliation
   711	    # (OpenSpec add-adaptive-model-router, D7/D10). None for CLI/SDK adapters.
   712	    generation_id: str | None = None
   713	    raw_stdout: str | None = None
   714	    raw_stderr: str | None = None
   715	    coercions: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
   716	    # Count of findings whose existing_code snippet did not resolve to a
   717	    # line_range (line_resolution="unresolved"). 0 when resolution did not
   718	    # run (no packet_diff available to _ingest_stdout) — see
   719	    # _extract_diff_from_prompt and line_resolver.resolve_all.
   720	    unanchored_findings: int = 0
   721	    # Per-vendor coverage scoring (add-deterministic-review-preprocessing,
   722	    # D5) — see _score_coverage. coverage_rate is None when the vendor
   723	    # reported no coverage block, or none could be scored (no selected-file
   724	    # list available); coverage_eligibility is "full" unless the rate fell
   725	    # below the contracted threshold; coverage_status is "unreported" unless
   726	    # a rate was actually computed.
   727	    coverage_rate: float | None = None
   728	    coverage_eligibility: str = "full"
   729	    coverage_status: str = "unreported"
   730	    # Exact lane and optional capacity metadata are additive for old callers.
   731	    agent_id: str | None = None
   732	    capacity_scope: str | None = None
   733	    capacity_model: str | None = None
   734	    capacity_reset_at: str | None = None
   735	    capacity_retry_after_seconds: int | None = None
   736	
   737	
   738	def _notify_capacity(
   739	    callback: Callable[[ReviewResult], Any] | None,
   740	    result: ReviewResult,
   741	) -> None:
   742	    """Keep optional reporting failures from changing dispatch outcomes."""
   743	    if callback is None:
   744	        return
   745	    try:
   746	        callback(result)
   747	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — reporting is best-effort
   748	        logger.warning(
   749	            "Capacity reporting failed for agent_id=%s: %s",
   750	            result.agent_id,
   751	            exc,
   752	        )
