   755	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   756	# Generic CLI adapter
   757	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   758	
   759	class CliVendorAdapter:
   760	    """Config-driven vendor adapter — one class handles all vendors."""
   761	
   762	    def __init__(
   763	        self,
   764	        agent_id: str,
   765	        vendor: str,
   766	        cli_config: CliConfig,
   767	        transport: str = "mcp",
   768	        ledger_submitter: Callable[..., dict[str, Any]] = try_submit_work,
   769	        ledger_completer: Callable[..., dict[str, Any]] = try_complete_work,
   770	    ) -> None:
   771	        self.agent_id = agent_id
   772	        self.vendor = vendor
   773	        self.cli_config = cli_config
   774	        self.transport = transport
   775	        self._ledger_submitter = ledger_submitter
   776	        self._ledger_completer = ledger_completer
   777	
   778	    @staticmethod
   779	    def _ledger_response_error(response: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
   780	        data = response.get("data")
   781	        reason = response.get("reason") or response.get("error")
   782	        if isinstance(data, dict):
   783	            reason = data.get("reason") or data.get("error") or reason
   784	        return str(reason or response.get("status") or "unknown ledger error")
   785	
   786	    def _open_completion_ledger(self, mode: str) -> tuple[str | None, str | None]:
   787	        """Create and claim one queue row before remote work can start."""
   788	        correlation_id = str(uuid4())
   789	        task_type = f"vendor-dispatch-{correlation_id}"
   790	        response = self._ledger_submitter(
   791	            task_type=task_type,
   792	            task_description=(
   793	                f"Track {self.agent_id} {mode} vendor dispatch {correlation_id}"
   794	            ),
   795	            input_data={
   796	                "correlation_id": correlation_id,
   797	                "vendor": self.vendor,
   798	                "vendor_agent_id": self.agent_id,
   799	                "dispatch_mode": mode,
   800	            },
   801	            priority=5,
   802	            claim_immediately=True,
   803	        )
   804	        data = response.get("data")
   805	        ledger_task_id = data.get("task_id") if isinstance(data, dict) else None
   806	        if (
   807	            response.get("status") != "ok"
   808	            or not isinstance(data, dict)
   809	            or data.get("success") is False
   810	            or not isinstance(ledger_task_id, str)
   811	            or not ledger_task_id
   812	        ):
   813	            return None, self._ledger_response_error(response)
   814	
   815	        if data.get("status") != "claimed":
   816	            return None, "atomic ledger submission did not return claimed status"
   817	        return ledger_task_id, None
   818	
   819	    def _complete_completion_ledger(
   820	        self,
   821	        ledger_task_id: str,
   822	        *,
   823	        success: bool,
   824	        envelope: VendorResultEnvelope | None = None,
   825	        error_message: str | None = None,
   826	    ) -> str | None:
   827	        """Persist terminal state and return an error when it was not recorded."""
   828	        result = (
   829	            {"vendor_result": envelope.as_dict()}
   830	            if envelope is not None
   831	            else None
   832	        )
   833	        response = self._ledger_completer(
   834	            task_id=ledger_task_id,
   835	            agent_id=None,
   836	            success=success,
   837	            result=result,
   838	            error_message=error_message,
   839	        )
   840	        data = response.get("data")
   841	        if (
   842	            response.get("status") != "ok"
   843	            or not isinstance(data, dict)
   844	            or data.get("success") is not True
   845	        ):
   846	            return self._ledger_response_error(response)
   847	        return None
   848	
   849	    def can_dispatch(self, mode: str) -> bool:
   850	        """Check if this adapter can dispatch the given mode.
   851	
   852	        A binary on PATH is not enough when the config declares a required
   853	        credential env var: pi with OPENROUTER_API_KEY unset cannot serve a
   854	        single request, so it must not count as available (issue #383).
   855	
   856	        The ocr vendor is a further special case: its configured
   857	        ``command`` is ``python3`` (the wrapper script's interpreter,
   858	        always present), which cannot itself indicate whether the `ocr`
   859	        binary and its LLM endpoint are actually available — see
   860	        ``_ocr_adapter_can_dispatch``.
   861	        """
   862	        if mode not in self.cli_config.dispatch_modes:
   863	            return False
   864	        if shutil.which(self.cli_config.command) is None:
   865	            return False
   866	        if self.cli_config.api_key_env and not os.environ.get(self.cli_config.api_key_env):
   867	            return False
   868	        if self.vendor == "ocr" and not _ocr_adapter_can_dispatch():
   869	            return False
   870	        return True
   871	
   872	    def _resolve_args(self, args: list[str]) -> list[str]:
   873	        """Expand config placeholders in a mode's args.
   874	
   875	        The grok schema sentinel (``@review-findings-schema``) is replaced with
   876	        the schema derived from the canonical ``review-findings.schema.json``.
   877	        This is what keeps agents.yaml from carrying a hand-copied — and
   878	        drift-prone — ``--json-schema`` blob: the schema is injected here from
   879	        the single canonical file at dispatch time.
   880	
   881	        Raises :class:`SchemaInjectionError` when the schema cannot be resolved.
   882	        Dropping ``--json-schema`` and dispatching anyway used to look like
   883	        graceful degradation, but grok only populates ``structuredOutput`` when
   884	        that flag is present (see the agents.yaml comment on the review mode) —
   885	        so the "degraded" path reliably produced output the dispatcher then
   886	        rejected as invalid JSON, while the real cause (an unresolvable
   887	        canonical schema) appeared only as a warning. Failing here names the
   888	        actual problem.
   889	        """
   890	        mod = _schema_mod()
   891	        sentinel = getattr(mod, "GROK_SCHEMA_SENTINEL", "@review-findings-schema")
   892	        if sentinel not in args:
   893	            return list(args)
   894	
   895	        if mod is None:
   896	            raise SchemaInjectionError(
   897	                "review_findings_schema module could not be loaded, so the "
   898	                f"{sentinel!r} placeholder in agents.yaml cannot be resolved"
   899	            )
   900	        try:
   901	            schema_arg = mod.grok_schema_arg()
   902	        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — re-raised with context
   903	            raise SchemaInjectionError(
   904	                f"could not derive the canonical review-findings schema: {exc}"
   905	            ) from exc
   906	
   907	        return [schema_arg if arg == sentinel else arg for arg in args]
   908	
   909	    def build_command(
   910	        self,
   911	        mode: str,
   912	        prompt: str,
   913	        model: str | None = None,
   914	        thinking: str | None = None,
   915	    ) -> list[str]:
   916	        """Build subprocess command from config.
   917	
   918	        When ``cli_config.prompt_via_stdin`` is True, the prompt is NOT
   919	        appended to the command — it will be passed via stdin instead.
   920	        When ``cli_config.prompt_via_flag`` is set, the prompt is attached as
   921	        the value of that flag (e.g. ``--prompt <prompt>``) and is neither a
   922	        trailing positional nor sent via stdin.
   923	
   924	        ``thinking`` is translated to vendor CLI flags from the authored
   925	        tier map (archetypes.yaml), not from hard-coded agents.yaml args.
   926	        """
   927	        mode_config = self.cli_config.dispatch_modes[mode]
   928	        cmd = [self.cli_config.command, *self._resolve_args(mode_config.args)]
   929	        # Drop any stale effort flags left in agents.yaml; tier thinking wins.
   930	        cmd = _strip_thinking_flags(self.vendor, cmd)
   931	        thinking_flags = _thinking_cli_flags(self.vendor, thinking)
   932	        if thinking_flags:
   933	            # Insert after the binary so mode flags still lead.
   934	            cmd[1:1] = thinking_flags
   935	        effective_model = model or self.cli_config.model
   936	        if effective_model:
   937	            cmd.extend([self.cli_config.model_flag, effective_model])
   938	        if self.cli_config.prompt_via_flag:
   939	            cmd.extend([self.cli_config.prompt_via_flag, prompt])
   940	        elif not self.cli_config.prompt_via_stdin:
   941	            cmd.append(prompt)
   942	        return cmd
   943	
   944	    def dispatch(
   945	        self,
   946	        mode: str,
   947	        prompt: str,
   948	        cwd: Path,
   949	        timeout_seconds: int = 300,
   950	        archetype_model: str | None = None,
   951	        thinking: str | None = None,
   952	        repair_attempted: bool = False,
   953	        capacity_callback: Callable[[ReviewResult], Any] | None = None,
   954	    ) -> ReviewResult:
   955	        """Dispatch a review with model fallback on capacity errors.
   956	
   957	        Tries the primary model first, then each fallback in order.
   958	        Returns the first successful result or the final failure.
   959	
   960	        Args:
   961	            archetype_model: Optional model override from archetype resolution.
   962	                When provided, overrides the agent's default primary model
   963	                but reuses the existing fallback chain (design decision D4).
   964	            thinking: Optional thinking/effort level from the tier map; when
   965	                omitted, resolved from archetypes.yaml premium for this vendor.
   966	        """
   967	        capacity_callback = capacity_callback or getattr(
   968	            self, "_capacity_callback", None
   969	        )
   970	        resolved_model, resolved_thinking = _resolve_review_model_spec(self.vendor)
   971	        primary = archetype_model or self.cli_config.model or resolved_model
   972	        effective_thinking = thinking if thinking is not None else resolved_thinking
   973	        models_to_try: list[str | None] = [primary]
   974	        # Prefer authored standard/economy tiers as capacity fallbacks when
   975	        # agents.yaml does not declare an explicit chain.
   976	        fallbacks = list(self.cli_config.model_fallbacks)
   977	        if not fallbacks:
   978	            fallbacks = _derived_tier_fallbacks(self.vendor)
   979	        models_to_try.extend(fallbacks)
   980	
   981	        models_attempted: list[str] = []
   982	        last_error = ""
   983	        last_error_class = ErrorClass.UNKNOWN
   984	        dispatch_start = time.monotonic()
   985	
   986	        for model_index, model in enumerate(models_to_try):
   987	            has_fallback = model_index < len(models_to_try) - 1
   988	            model_name = model or "(default)"
   989	            models_attempted.append(model_name)
   990	
   991	            try:
   992	                cmd = self.build_command(
   993	                    mode, prompt, model, thinking=effective_thinking
   994	                )
   995	            except SchemaInjectionError as exc:
   996	                # Fail this vendor, not the whole panel: the other vendors'
   997	                # dispatches are independent and a partial panel beats none.
   998	                # Retrying the fallback models would not help — schema
   999	                # resolution is model-independent.
  1000	                return ReviewResult(
  1001	                    vendor=self.vendor,
  1002	                    success=False,
  1003	                    models_attempted=models_attempted,
  1004	                    elapsed_seconds=time.monotonic() - dispatch_start,
  1005	                    error=f"Schema injection failed: {exc}",
  1006	                    error_class=ErrorClass.UNKNOWN,
  1007	                )
  1008	            stdin_text = prompt if self.cli_config.prompt_via_stdin else None
  1009	            start = time.monotonic()
  1010	
  1011	            try:
  1012	                result = subprocess.run(
  1013	                    cmd,
  1014	                    input=stdin_text,
  1015	                    capture_output=True,
  1016	                    text=True,
  1017	                    timeout=timeout_seconds,
  1018	                    cwd=str(cwd),
  1019	                )
  1020	                elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
  1021	
  1022	                if result.returncode == 0:
  1023	                    ingested = self._ingest_stdout(
  1024	                        result.stdout,
  1025	                        result.stderr,
  1026	                        elapsed=elapsed,
  1027	                        model_name=model_name,
  1028	                        models_attempted=models_attempted,
  1029	                        packet_diff=_extract_diff_from_prompt(prompt),
  1030	                        selected_files=_extract_selected_files_from_prompt(prompt),
  1031	                        coverage_quorum_threshold=_coverage_quorum_threshold(cwd),
  1032	                    )
  1033	                    if ingested.success or ingested.error_class in (
  1034	                        ErrorClass.AUTH, ErrorClass.UNAVAILABLE,
  1035	                    ):
  1036	                        return ingested
  1037	                    if ingested.error == "non_substantive_placeholder":
  1038	                        return ingested
  1039	                    if ingested.error_class == ErrorClass.CAPACITY:
  1040	                        last_error = ingested.error or ""
  1041	                        last_error_class = ErrorClass.CAPACITY
  1042	                        if has_fallback and capacity_callback is not None:
  1043	                            _notify_capacity(capacity_callback, ReviewResult(
  1044	                                vendor=self.vendor,
  1045	                                success=False,
  1046	                                agent_id=self.agent_id,
  1047	                                error=last_error,
  1048	                                error_class=ErrorClass.CAPACITY,
  1049	                                capacity_scope="model",
  1050	                                capacity_model=model_name,
  1051	                            ))
  1052	                        continue
  1053	                    if not repair_attempted:
  1054	                        repair_prompt = (
  1055	                            f"{prompt}\n\nPREVIOUS OUTPUT FAILED VALIDATION:\n"
  1056	                            f"{ingested.error or 'not valid JSON'}\n"
  1057	                            "Emit ONLY a JSON object with a top-level `findings` "
  1058	                            "array. No prose.\n"
  1059	                        )
  1060	                        return self.dispatch(
  1061	                            mode,
  1062	                            repair_prompt,
  1063	                            cwd,
  1064	                            timeout_seconds=timeout_seconds,
  1065	                            archetype_model=archetype_model,
  1066	                            repair_attempted=True,
  1067	                            capacity_callback=capacity_callback,
  1068	                        )
  1069	                    return ingested
  1070	                else:
  1071	                    # Non-zero exit — classify error
  1072	                    last_error = result.stderr
  1073	                    last_error_class = classify_error(result.stderr)
  1074	
  1075	                if last_error_class in (ErrorClass.AUTH, ErrorClass.UNAVAILABLE):
  1076	                    # Neither auth nor billing/entitlement errors can be fixed
  1077	                    # by model fallback — they are account-scoped.
  1078	                    relogin = _relogin_hint(self.cli_config.command)
  1079	                    if last_error_class == ErrorClass.AUTH:
  1080	                        summary = f"Auth expired. Run: {relogin}"
  1081	                    else:
  1082	                        summary = (
  1083	                            f"Vendor unavailable (billing/credits): "
  1084	                            f"{last_error[:500] if last_error else 'no error output'}"
  1085	                        )
  1086	                    msg = (
  1087	                        f"[WARN] {self.vendor} review failed: "
  1088	                        f"{last_error_class.value}.\n       {summary}"
  1089	                    )
  1090	                    print(msg, file=sys.stderr)
  1091	                    return ReviewResult(
  1092	                        vendor=self.vendor,
  1093	                        success=False,
  1094	                        models_attempted=models_attempted,
  1095	                        elapsed_seconds=time.monotonic() - start,
  1096	                        error=summary,
  1097	                        error_class=last_error_class,
  1098	                    )
  1099	
  1100	                if last_error_class == ErrorClass.CAPACITY:
  1101	                    # Report this model before fallback; final success must not erase it.
  1102	                    if has_fallback and capacity_callback is not None:
  1103	                        _notify_capacity(capacity_callback, ReviewResult(
  1104	                            vendor=self.vendor,
  1105	                            success=False,
  1106	                            agent_id=self.agent_id,
  1107	                            error=last_error[:500] if last_error else "capacity_exhausted",
  1108	                            error_class=ErrorClass.CAPACITY,
  1109	                            capacity_scope="model",
  1110	                            capacity_model=model_name,
  1111	                        ))
  1112	                    logger.info(
  1113	                        "%s model %s capacity exhausted, trying fallback",
  1114	                        self.vendor, model_name,
  1115	                    )
  1116	                    continue
  1117	
  1118	                # Non-capacity, non-auth error — don't retry
  1119	                break
  1120	
  1400	            if not isinstance(obj, dict):
  1401	                continue
  1402	            saw_event = True
  1403	            direct = CliVendorAdapter._extract_findings(obj)
  1404	            if direct is not None:
  1405	                return direct
  1406	            assistant_text = CliVendorAdapter._assistant_text(obj.get("message"))
  1407	            if assistant_text:
  1408	                last_assistant_text = assistant_text
  1409	
  1410	        if not saw_event or last_assistant_text is None:
  1411	            return None
  1412	        return CliVendorAdapter._parse_json_blob(last_assistant_text)
  1413	
  1414	    @staticmethod
  1415	    def _parse_findings(stdout: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
  1416	        """Try to parse review findings JSON from stdout.
  1417	
  1418	        Handles a bare JSON object, prose wrapped around the JSON, vendor
  1419	        envelopes (e.g. grok ``--output-format json`` nesting the object under
  1420	        ``structuredOutput``), and NDJSON event streams (e.g. pi ``--mode
  1421	        json``) that carry the answer inside assistant message events.
  1422	        """
  1423	        text = stdout.strip()
  1424	        if not text:
  1425	            return None
  1426	        result = CliVendorAdapter._parse_json_blob(text)
  1427	        if result is not None:
  1428	            return result
  1429	        return CliVendorAdapter._parse_ndjson_findings(text)
  1430	
  1431	    def dispatch_async(
  1432	        self,
  1433	        mode: str,
  1434	        prompt: str,
  1435	        cwd: Path,
  1436	        capacity_callback: Callable[[ReviewResult], Any] | None = None,
  1437	    ) -> ReviewResult:
  1438	        """Open a ledger lifecycle, submit remote work, and return both IDs."""
  1439	        capacity_callback = capacity_callback or getattr(
  1440	            self, "_capacity_callback", None
  1441	        )
  1442	        mode_config = self.cli_config.dispatch_modes[mode]
  1443	        if not mode_config.async_dispatch or not mode_config.poll:
  1444	            return ReviewResult(
  1445	                vendor=self.vendor, success=False,
  1446	                error="Mode is not configured for async dispatch",
  1447	            )
  1448	        if mode_config.poll.result_protocol != "vendor-envelope-v1":
  1449	            return ReviewResult(
  1450	                vendor=self.vendor,
  1451	                success=False,
  1452	                error=(
  1453	                    "Unsupported result protocol: "
  1454	                    f"{mode_config.poll.result_protocol}"
  1455	                ),
  1456	            )
  1457	
  1458	        ledger_task_id, ledger_error = self._open_completion_ledger(mode)
  1459	        if ledger_task_id is None:
  1460	            return ReviewResult(
  1461	                vendor=self.vendor,
  1462	                success=False,
  1463	                error=f"Completion ledger submission failed: {ledger_error}",
  1464	                error_class=ErrorClass.UNKNOWN,
  1465	            )
  1466	
  1467	        def fail(
  1468	            message: str,
  1469	            *,
  1470	            error_class: ErrorClass = ErrorClass.UNKNOWN,
  1471	            elapsed: float = 0.0,
  1472	            envelope: VendorResultEnvelope | None = None,
  1473	        ) -> ReviewResult:
  1474	            completion_error = self._complete_completion_ledger(
  1475	                ledger_task_id,
  1476	                success=False,
  1477	                envelope=envelope,
  1478	                error_message=message,
  1479	            )
  1480	            if completion_error:
  1481	                message = (
  1482	                    f"{message}; completion ledger update failed: "
  1483	                    f"{completion_error}"
  1484	                )
  1485	            return ReviewResult(
  1486	                vendor=self.vendor,
  1487	                success=False,
  1488	                models_attempted=models_attempted,
  1489	                elapsed_seconds=elapsed,
  1490	                error=message,
  1491	                error_class=error_class,
  1492	                ledger_task_id=ledger_task_id,
  1493	            )
  1494	
  1495	        # Model fallback: prefer archetype premium, then agents.yaml, then tiers.
  1496	        resolved_model, resolved_thinking = _resolve_review_model_spec(self.vendor)
  1497	        primary = self.cli_config.model or resolved_model
  1498	        models_to_try: list[str | None] = [primary]
  1499	        fallbacks = list(self.cli_config.model_fallbacks) or _derived_tier_fallbacks(
  1500	            self.vendor
  1501	        )
  1502	        models_to_try.extend(fallbacks)
  1503	
  1504	        models_attempted: list[str] = []
  1505	
  1506	        for model_index, model in enumerate(models_to_try):
  1507	            has_fallback = model_index < len(models_to_try) - 1
  1508	            model_name = model or "(default)"
  1509	            models_attempted.append(model_name)
  1510	
  1511	            try:
  1512	                cmd = self.build_command(
  1513	                    mode, prompt, model, thinking=resolved_thinking
  1514	                )
  1515	            except SchemaInjectionError as exc:
  1516	                # Same posture as the sync path: fail this vendor loudly rather
  1517	                # than submitting a schema-less async task whose result would
  1518	                # be unparseable for a reason the logs never name.
  1519	                return fail(
  1520	                    f"Schema injection failed: {exc}",
  1521	                )
  1522	            stdin_text = prompt if self.cli_config.prompt_via_stdin else None
  1523	            start = time.monotonic()
  1524	
  1525	            try:
  1526	                result = subprocess.run(
  1527	                    cmd,
  1528	                    input=stdin_text,
  1529	                    capture_output=True,
  1530	                    text=True,
  1531	                    timeout=120,  # submit timeout (not execution timeout)
  1532	                    cwd=str(cwd),
  1533	                )
  1534	            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
  1535	                return fail(
  1536	                    "Timeout submitting async task",
  1537	                    error_class=ErrorClass.TRANSIENT,
  1538	                )
  1539	            except OSError as exc:
  1540	                return fail(
  1541	                    f"Async submission command failed: {exc}",
  1542	                    error_class=ErrorClass.UNKNOWN,
  1543	                    elapsed=time.monotonic() - start,
  1544	                )
  1545	
  1546	            elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
  1547	
  1548	            # Process errors before reading the structured envelope.
  1549	            if result.returncode != 0:
  1550	                error_class = classify_error(result.stderr)
  1551	                if error_class == ErrorClass.AUTH:
  1552	                    relogin = _relogin_hint(self.cli_config.command)
  1553	                    print(
  1554	                        f"[WARN] {self.vendor} async dispatch failed: "
  1555	                        f"auth expired.\n       Run: {relogin}",
  1556	                        file=sys.stderr,
  1557	                    )
  1558	                    return fail(
  1559	                        f"Auth expired. Run: {relogin}",
  1560	                        error_class=ErrorClass.AUTH,
  1561	                        elapsed=elapsed,
  1562	                    )
  1563	                if error_class == ErrorClass.CAPACITY:
  1564	                    if has_fallback and capacity_callback is not None:
  1565	                        _notify_capacity(capacity_callback, ReviewResult(
  1566	                            vendor=self.vendor,
  1567	                            success=False,
  1568	                            agent_id=self.agent_id,
  1569	                            error=result.stderr[:500] or "capacity_exhausted",
  1570	                            error_class=ErrorClass.CAPACITY,
  1571	                            capacity_scope="model",
  1572	                            capacity_model=model_name,
  1573	                        ))
  1574	                    logger.info(
  1575	                        "%s async model %s capacity exhausted%s",
  1576	                        self.vendor,
  1577	                        model_name,
  1578	                        ", trying fallback" if has_fallback else "",
  1579	                    )
  1580	                    continue
  1581	                # Non-retryable error
  1582	                return fail(
  1583	                    result.stderr[:500] or "async submission command failed",
  1584	                    error_class=error_class,
  1585	                    elapsed=elapsed,
  1586	                )
  1587	
  1588	            try:
  1589	                envelope = parse_vendor_result_envelope(result.stdout)
  1590	            except VendorResultProtocolError as exc:
  1591	                return fail(
  1592	                    f"Invalid structured async submission: {exc}",
  1593	                    elapsed=elapsed,
  1594	                )
  1595	            if envelope.is_terminal:
  1596	                return fail(
  1597	                    (envelope.error or {}).get(
  1598	                        "message", "async submission was terminal"
  1599	                    ),
  1600	                    elapsed=elapsed,
  1601	                    envelope=envelope,
  1602	                )
  1603	            logger.info(
  1604	                "Async task submitted for %s: vendor_task_id=%s ledger_task_id=%s",
  1605	                self.vendor,
  1606	                envelope.vendor_task_id,
  1607	                ledger_task_id,
  1608	            )
  1609	            return ReviewResult(
  1610	                vendor=self.vendor,
  1611	                success=True,
  1612	                models_attempted=models_attempted,
  1613	                elapsed_seconds=elapsed,
  1614	                async_dispatch=True,
  1615	                task_id=envelope.vendor_task_id,
  1616	                ledger_task_id=ledger_task_id,
  1617	            )
  1618	
  1619	        # All models exhausted
  1620	        return fail(
  1621	            "All models exhausted for async dispatch",
  1622	            error_class=ErrorClass.CAPACITY,
  1623	        )
  1624	
  1625	    def poll_for_result(
  1626	        self,
  1627	        task_id: str,
  1628	        poll_config: PollConfig,
  1629	        cwd: Path | None = None,
  1630	        *,
  1631	        review_started_at: float | None = None,
  1632	        ledger_task_id: str | None = None,
  1633	    ) -> ReviewResult:
  1634	        """Poll structured status and persist terminal state before ingestion.
  1635	
  1636	        Args:
  1637	            task_id: Vendor task identifier from the submission envelope.
  1638	            poll_config: Polling configuration from the mode config.
  1639	            cwd: Working directory for poll commands (optional).
  1640	            review_started_at: Local monotonic timestamp from before submission,
  1641	                when the caller owns the submission lifecycle.
  1642	            ledger_task_id: Coordinator work id created before vendor launch.
  1643	
  1644	        Returns:
  1645	            ReviewResult with findings if successful, error otherwise.
  1646	        """
  1647	        if not ledger_task_id:
  1648	            return ReviewResult(
  1649	                vendor=self.vendor,
  1650	                success=False,
  1651	                error="Completion ledger task id is required for async polling",
  1652	                error_class=ErrorClass.UNKNOWN,
  1653	                task_id=task_id,
  1654	            )
  1655	
  1656	        poll_cmd = [
  1657	            arg.replace("{task_id}", task_id)
  1658	            for arg in poll_config.command_template
  1659	        ]
  1660	
  1661	        start = time.monotonic()
  1662	        elapsed_start = review_started_at if review_started_at is not None else start
  1663	        deadline = start + poll_config.timeout_seconds
  1664	        attempts = 0
  1665	
  1666	        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
  1667	            attempts += 1
  1668	            logger.info(
  1669	                "Polling %s task %s (attempt %d)", self.vendor, task_id, attempts,
  1670	            )
  1671	
  1672	            try:
  1673	                result = subprocess.run(
  1674	                    poll_cmd,
  1675	                    capture_output=True,
  1676	                    text=True,
  1677	                    timeout=30,
  1678	                    cwd=str(cwd) if cwd else None,
  1679	                )
  1680	            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
  1681	                logger.warning("Poll command timed out, retrying")
  1682	                time.sleep(poll_config.interval_seconds)
  1683	                continue
  1684	            except OSError as exc:
  1685	                message = f"Async status command failed: {exc}"
  1686	                ledger_error = self._complete_completion_ledger(
  1687	                    ledger_task_id,
  1688	                    success=False,
  1689	                    error_message=message,
  1690	                )
  1691	                if ledger_error:
  1692	                    message += f"; completion ledger update failed: {ledger_error}"
  1693	                return ReviewResult(
  1694	                    vendor=self.vendor,
  1695	                    success=False,
  1696	                    elapsed_seconds=time.monotonic() - elapsed_start,
  1697	                    error=message,
  1698	                    error_class=ErrorClass.UNKNOWN,
  1699	                    task_id=task_id,
  1700	                    ledger_task_id=ledger_task_id,
  1701	                )
  1702	
  1703	            if result.returncode != 0:
  1704	                message = result.stderr[:500] or "async status command failed"
  1705	                ledger_error = self._complete_completion_ledger(
  1706	                    ledger_task_id,
  1707	                    success=False,
  1708	                    error_message=message,
  1709	                )
  1710	                if ledger_error:
  1711	                    message += f"; completion ledger update failed: {ledger_error}"
  1712	                return ReviewResult(
  1713	                    vendor=self.vendor,
  1714	                    success=False,
  1715	                    elapsed_seconds=time.monotonic() - elapsed_start,
  1716	                    error=message,
  1717	                    error_class=classify_error(result.stderr),
  1718	                    task_id=task_id,
  1719	                    ledger_task_id=ledger_task_id,
  1720	                )
  1721	            try:
  1722	                envelope = parse_vendor_result_envelope(result.stdout)
  1723	            except VendorResultProtocolError as exc:
  1724	                message = f"Invalid structured async status: {exc}"
  1725	                ledger_error = self._complete_completion_ledger(
  1726	                    ledger_task_id,
  1727	                    success=False,
  1728	                    error_message=message,
  1729	                )
  1730	                if ledger_error:
  1731	                    message += f"; completion ledger update failed: {ledger_error}"
  1732	                return ReviewResult(
  1733	                    vendor=self.vendor,
  1734	                    success=False,
  1735	                    elapsed_seconds=time.monotonic() - elapsed_start,
  1736	                    error=message,
  1737	                    error_class=ErrorClass.UNKNOWN,
  1738	                    task_id=task_id,
  1739	                    ledger_task_id=ledger_task_id,
  1740	                )
  2340	
  2341	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2342	# Detached snapshot fallback for concurrent git-index errors (D2)
  2343	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2344	
  2345	# Substring markers — same style as classify_error, not a result-path regex.
  2346	_GIT_INDEX_ERROR_MARKERS = (
  2347	    "index.lock",
  2348	    "unable to access index",
  2349	    "another git process",
  2350	)
  2351	
  2352	
  2353	def _is_concurrent_git_error(result: ReviewResult) -> bool:
  2354	    """True when a vendor CLI failed because of concurrent git index access."""
  2355	    blob = "\n".join(
  2356	        part for part in (result.error, result.raw_stderr, result.raw_stdout) if part
  2357	    ).lower()
  2358	    return any(marker in blob for marker in _GIT_INDEX_ERROR_MARKERS)
  2359	
  2360	
  2361	def _safe_path_component(value: str) -> str:
  2362	    cleaned = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+", "_", value).strip("._-")
  2363	    return cleaned or "unknown"
  2364	
  2365	
  2366	def _round_id_from_packet(packet_path: Path | None) -> str:
  2367	    if packet_path is None:
  2368	        return "default"
  2369	    name = Path(packet_path).parent.name
  2370	    return _safe_path_component(name) if name else "default"
  2371	
  2372	
  2373	def _main_repo_from_cwd(cwd: Path) -> Path:
  2374	    """Resolve the main repository root even when *cwd* is a linked worktree."""
  2375	    try:
  2376	        proc = subprocess.run(
  2377	            ["git", "rev-parse", "--git-common-dir"],
  2378	            cwd=str(cwd),
  2379	            capture_output=True,
  2380	            text=True,
  2381	            timeout=15,
  2382	        )
  2383	    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
  2384	        return Path(cwd)
  2385	    if proc.returncode != 0 or not proc.stdout.strip():
  2386	        return Path(cwd)
  2387	    git_common = proc.stdout.strip()
  2388	    if git_common == ".git":
  2389	        try:
  2390	            top = subprocess.run(
  2391	                ["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"],
  2392	                cwd=str(cwd),
  2393	                capture_output=True,
  2394	                text=True,
  2395	                timeout=15,
  2396	            )
  2397	        except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
  2398	            return Path(cwd)
  2399	        if top.returncode == 0 and top.stdout.strip():
  2400	            return Path(top.stdout.strip())
  2401	        return Path(cwd)
  2402	    common_path = Path(git_common)
  2403	    if not common_path.is_absolute():
  2404	        common_path = (Path(cwd) / common_path).resolve()
  2405	    if common_path.name == ".git":
  2406	        return common_path.parent
  2407	    return common_path
  2408	
  2409	
  2410	def review_snapshot_path(cwd: Path, round_id: str, vendor: str) -> Path:
  2411	    """``.git-worktrees/.review-snapshots/<round>/<vendor>/`` under the main repo."""
  2412	    root = _main_repo_from_cwd(cwd) / ".git-worktrees" / ".review-snapshots"
  2413	    return root / _safe_path_component(round_id) / _safe_path_component(vendor)
  2414	
  2415	
  2416	def create_review_snapshot(cwd: Path, round_id: str, vendor: str) -> Path:
  2417	    """Add a detached throwaway worktree for one vendor retry, then return it."""
  2418	    dest = review_snapshot_path(cwd, round_id, vendor)
  2419	    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  2420	    if dest.exists():
  2421	        destroy_review_snapshot(dest, cwd)
  2422	    subprocess.run(
  2423	        ["git", "worktree", "add", "--detach", str(dest), "HEAD"],
  2424	        cwd=str(cwd),
  2425	        check=True,
  2426	        capture_output=True,
  2427	        text=True,
  2428	        timeout=60,
  2429	    )
  2430	    return dest
  2431	
  2432	
  2433	def destroy_review_snapshot(snapshot: Path, git_cwd: Path) -> None:
  2434	    """Remove a review snapshot worktree after collect. Best-effort."""
  2435	    try:
  2436	        subprocess.run(
  2437	            ["git", "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(snapshot)],
  2438	            cwd=str(git_cwd),
  2439	            capture_output=True,
  2440	            text=True,
  2441	            timeout=60,
  2442	            check=False,
  2443	        )
  2444	    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as exc:
  2445	        logger.warning("Failed to remove review snapshot %s: %s", snapshot, exc)
  2446	    if Path(snapshot).exists():
  2447	        shutil.rmtree(snapshot, ignore_errors=True)
  2448	    try:
  2449	        subprocess.run(
  2450	            ["git", "worktree", "prune"],
  2451	            cwd=str(git_cwd),
  2452	            capture_output=True,
  2453	            text=True,
  2454	            timeout=30,
  2455	            check=False,
  2456	        )
  2457	    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired):
  2458	        pass
  2459	
  2460	
  2461	def _dispatch_with_snapshot_fallback(
  2462	    *,
  2463	    vendor: str,
  2464	    cwd: Path,
  2465	    round_id: str,
  2466	    run: Callable[[Path], ReviewResult],
  2467	) -> ReviewResult:
  2468	    """Run *run(cwd)*; on concurrent git-index failure, retry on a snapshot."""
  2469	    result = run(cwd)
  2470	    if result.success or not _is_concurrent_git_error(result):
  2471	        return result
  2472	    logger.warning(
  2473	        "Concurrent git access error for %s; retrying on detached snapshot",
  2474	        vendor,
  2475	    )
  2476	    snapshot: Path | None = None
  2477	    try:
  2478	        snapshot = create_review_snapshot(cwd, round_id, vendor)
  2479	        return run(snapshot)
  2480	    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — keep the original vendor error
  2481	        logger.warning("Snapshot fallback failed for %s: %s", vendor, exc)
  2482	        return result
  2483	    finally:
  2484	        if snapshot is not None:
  2485	            destroy_review_snapshot(snapshot, cwd)
  2486

  2488	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2489	# Review orchestrator
  2490	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  2491	
  2492	class ReviewOrchestrator:
  2493	    """Multi-vendor review dispatch orchestrator.
  2494	
  2495	    Supports CLI, SDK, and OpenAI-compatible adapters with ordered selection:
  2496	    Tier 1 (Local CLI) → Tier 2 (SDK/API) → Tier 2.5 (OpenAI-compatible)
  2497	    → Tier 3 (Skip).
  2498	    """
  2499	
  2500	    def __init__(
  2501	        self,
  2502	        adapters: dict[str, CliVendorAdapter],
  2503	        sdk_adapters: dict[str, SdkVendorAdapter] | None = None,
  2504	        openai_adapters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
  2505	        openai_key_envs: dict[str, str] | None = None,
  2710	        and Python binary from it.  Returns ``(python_bin, ac_dir)`` or
  2711	        ``None`` if not configured.
  2712	        """
  2713	        claude_json = Path.home() / ".claude.json"
  2714	        if not claude_json.is_file():
  2715	            return None
  2716	        try:
  2717	            cfg = json.loads(claude_json.read_text())
  2718	            mcp = cfg.get("mcpServers", {}).get("coordination", {})
  2719	            python_bin = mcp.get("command", "")
  2720	            args = mcp.get("args", [])
  2721	            if not python_bin or not args:
  2722	                return None
  2723	            # args[0] is the path to run_mcp.py; its parent is agent-coordinator
  2724	            ac_dir = Path(args[0]).resolve().parent
  2725	            if not ac_dir.is_dir():
  2726	                return None
  2727	            return (python_bin, ac_dir)
  2728	        except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError, IndexError):
  2729	            return None
  2730	
  2731	    @classmethod
  2732	    def from_coordinator(cls) -> "ReviewOrchestrator":
  2733	        """Create orchestrator using provider-neutral discovery order."""
  2734	        explicit = cls._explicit_agents_yaml_path()
  2735	        if explicit:
  2736	            data = cls._config_from_agents_yaml(explicit)
  2737	            if data is not None:
  2738	                return cls.from_config_dict(data)
  2739	
  2740	        data = cls._load_from_http()
  2741	        if data is not None:
  2742	            return cls.from_config_dict(data)
  2743	
  2744	        # Provider-native fallback. Today this includes Claude Code MCP config.
  2745	        found = cls._find_coordinator_dir()
  2746	        if found:
  2747	            python_bin, ac_dir = found
  2748	            script = ac_dir / "get_dispatch_configs.py"
  2749	            if script.is_file():
  2750	                try:
  2751	                    result = subprocess.run(
  2752	                        [python_bin, str(script)],
  2753	                        capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15,
  2754	                    )
  2755	                    if result.returncode == 0:
  2756	                        return cls.from_config_dict(json.loads(result.stdout))
  2757	                    logger.warning("Coordinator query failed: %s", result.stderr[:200])
  2758	                except (subprocess.TimeoutExpired, json.JSONDecodeError, OSError) as exc:
  2759	                    logger.warning("Coordinator query error: %s", exc)
  2760	
  2761	        # Compatibility only: source-repository configuration is considered
  2762	        # after explicit, HTTP, and provider-native MCP configuration.
  2763	        local = cls._find_local_agents_yaml()
  2764	        if local:
  2765	            data = cls._config_from_agents_yaml(local)
  2766	            if data is not None:
  2767	                return cls.from_config_dict(data)
  2768	
  2769	        logger.warning("No public or local vendor configuration found")
  2770	        return cls({})
  2771	
  2772	    @classmethod
  2773	    def from_agents_yaml(cls, path: Path | None = None) -> "ReviewOrchestrator":
  2774	        """Create orchestrator from explicit or local agents.yaml."""
  2775	        resolved = path or cls._explicit_agents_yaml_path() or cls._find_local_agents_yaml()
  2776	        if resolved is None:
  2777	            logger.warning("agents.yaml not found via explicit path or local repo fallback")
  2778	            return cls({})
  2779	        data = cls._config_from_agents_yaml(resolved)
  2780	        if data is None:
  2781	            return cls({})
  2782	        try:
  2783	            return cls.from_config_dict(data)
  2784	        except (KeyError, TypeError) as exc:
  2785	            logger.warning("agents.yaml dispatch config conversion failed: %s", exc)

   917

   920	        When ``cli_config.prompt_via_flag`` is set, the prompt is attached as

   944	    def dispatch(
   945	        self,
   946	        mode: str,
   947	        prompt: str,
   948	        cwd: Path,

   955	        """Dispatch a review with model fallback on capacity errors.
   956

   968	            self, "_capacity_callback", None

   971	        primary = archetype_model or self.cli_config.model or resolved_model
   972	        effective_thinking = thinking if thinking is not None else resolved_thinking

   975	        # agents.yaml does not declare an explicit chain.

   977	        if not fallbacks:
   978	            fallbacks = _derived_tier_fallbacks(self.vendor)
   979	        models_to_try.extend(fallbacks)

   983	        last_error_class = ErrorClass.UNKNOWN
   984	        dispatch_start = time.monotonic()
   985

   987	            has_fallback = model_index < len(models_to_try) - 1

   989	            models_attempted.append(model_name)

   992	                cmd = self.build_command(
   993	                    mode, prompt, model, thinking=effective_thinking
   994	                )
   995	            except SchemaInjectionError as exc:
   996	                # Fail this vendor, not the whole panel: the other vendors'
   997	                # dispatches are independent and a partial panel beats none.
   998	                # Retrying the fallback models would not help — schema
   999	                # resolution is model-independent.
  1000	                return ReviewResult(
  1001	                    vendor=self.vendor,
  1002	                    success=False,

  1415	    def _parse_findings(stdout: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
  1416	        """Try to parse review findings JSON from stdout.
  1417	
  1418	        Handles a bare JSON object, prose wrapped around the JSON, vendor
  1419	        envelopes (e.g. grok ``--output-format json`` nesting the object under
  1420	        ``structuredOutput``), and NDJSON event streams (e.g. pi ``--mode

  1424	        if not text:
  1425	            return None
  1426	        result = CliVendorAdapter._parse_json_blob(text)
  1427	        if result is not None:
  1428	            return result

  1431	    def dispatch_async(

   474	def _run_local_agent_cli(
   475	    payload: PhaseDispatchPayload,
   476	) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
   477	    """Run Pi headlessly with the local endpoint registered as a provider."""
   478	    if not _LOCAL_PI_EXTENSION.is_file():
   479	        raise LocalAdapterError("local Pi provider extension is missing")
   480	    env = os.environ.copy()
   481	    env["LOCAL_INFERENCE_MODEL"] = payload.model or ""
   482	    command = [
   483	        "pi",
   484	        "-p",
   485	        "--provider",
   486	        "local",
   487	        "--model",
   488	        payload.model or "",
   489	        "--mode",
   490	        "json",
   491	        "--approve",
   492	        "--no-session",
   493	        "--extension",
   494	        str(_LOCAL_PI_EXTENSION),
   495	        _local_harness_prompt(payload),
   496	    ]
   497	    return subprocess.run(  # noqa: S603 -- fixed executable and list-form args
   498	        command,
   499	        capture_output=True,
   500	        text=True,
   501	        timeout=_LOCAL_DISPATCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
   502	        env=env,
   503	        check=False,
   504	    )

   507	def _assistant_text(message: Any) -> str | None:
   508	    """Extract assistant text from a Pi JSON-mode message payload."""
   509	    if not isinstance(message, dict) or message.get("role") != "assistant":
   510	        return None
   511	    content = message.get("content")
   512	    if isinstance(content, str):
   513	        return content
   514	    if isinstance(content, list):
   515	        parts = [
   516	            part["text"]
   517	            for part in content
   518	            if isinstance(part, dict) and isinstance(part.get("text"), str)
   519	        ]
   520	        return chr(10).join(parts) if parts else None

     2	
     3	Executes tasks via the Codex CLI and captures results.
     4	"""
     5	
     6	from __future__ import annotations
     7	
     8	import asyncio
     9	import os
    10	import shutil
    11	import time
    12	
    13	from ..config import AblationFlags, AgentBackendConfig
    14	from ..metrics import TokenUsage
    15	from .base import BackendResult
    16	
    17	
    18	class CodexBackend:
    19	    """Backend that executes tasks via Codex CLI."""
    20	
    21	    def __init__(
    22	        self,
    23	        command: str = "codex",
    24	        args: list[str] | None = None,
    25	        env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    26	        timeout_seconds: int = 300,
    27	    ) -> None:
    28	        self._command = command
    29	        self._args = args or []
    30	        self._env = env or {}
    31	        self._timeout = timeout_seconds
    32	
    33	    @property
    34	    def name(self) -> str:
    35	        return "codex"
    36	
    37	    async def execute_task(
    38	        self,
    39	        task_description: str,
    40	        affected_files: list[str],
    41	        working_dir: str,
    42	        ablation: AblationFlags,
    43	        timeout_seconds: int = 300,
    44	    ) -> BackendResult:
    45	        """Execute a task via codex CLI."""
    46	        timeout = timeout_seconds if timeout_seconds is not None else self._timeout
    47	        start_time = time.time()
    48	
    49	        files_context = "\n".join(f"- {f}" for f in affected_files)
    50	        prompt = f"{task_description}\n\nFiles to work on:\n{files_context}"
    51	
    52	        cmd = [self._command, *self._args, prompt]
    53	
    54	        try:
    55	            env = {**os.environ, **self._env}
    56	            process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
    57	                *cmd,
    58	                stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
    59	                stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
    60	                cwd=working_dir,
    61	                env=env,
    62	            )
    63	            stdout, stderr = await asyncio.wait_for(
    64	                process.communicate(), timeout=timeout
    65	            )
    66	            wall_clock = time.time() - start_time
    67	
    68	            output = stdout.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    69	            err_output = stderr.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    70	
    71	            return BackendResult(
    72	                success=process.returncode == 0,
    73	                output=output,
    74	                wall_clock_seconds=wall_clock,
    75	                token_usage=TokenUsage(),
    76	                error=err_output if process.returncode != 0 else None,
    77	            )
    78	        except TimeoutError:
    79	            return BackendResult(

     1	"""Claude Code agent backend for evaluation.
     2	
     3	Executes tasks via the Claude Code CLI (`claude` command)

    19	class ClaudeCodeBackend:
    20	    """Backend that executes tasks via Claude Code CLI."""
    21	
    22	    def __init__(
    23	        self,
    24	        command: str = "claude",
    25	        args: list[str] | None = None,
    26	        env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    27	        timeout_seconds: int = 300,
    28	    ) -> None:
    29	        self._command = command
    30	        self._args = args or []
    31	        self._env = env or {}
    32	        self._timeout = timeout_seconds
    33	
    34	    @property
    35	    def name(self) -> str:
    36	        return "claude_code"
    37	
    38	    async def execute_task(
    39	        self,
    40	        task_description: str,
    41	        affected_files: list[str],
    42	        working_dir: str,
    43	        ablation: AblationFlags,
    44	        timeout_seconds: int = 300,
    45	    ) -> BackendResult:
    46	        """Execute a task via claude CLI with --print flag."""
    47	        timeout = timeout_seconds if timeout_seconds is not None else self._timeout
    48	        start_time = time.time()
    49	
    50	        # Build the prompt with file context
    51	        files_context = "\n".join(f"- {f}" for f in affected_files)
    52	        prompt = f"""{task_description}
    53	
    54	Files to work on:
    55	{files_context}
    56	
    57	Coordination config:
    58	- Locking: {"enabled" if ablation.locking else "disabled"}
    59	- Memory: {"enabled" if ablation.memory else "disabled"}
    60	- Parallelization: {"enabled" if ablation.parallelization else "disabled"}
    61	"""
    62	
    63	        cmd = [self._command, "--print", *self._args, prompt]
    64	
    65	        try:
    66	            env = {**os.environ, **self._env}
    67	            process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
    68	                *cmd,
    69	                stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
    70	                stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
    71	                cwd=working_dir,
    72	                env=env,
    73	            )
    74	            stdout, stderr = await asyncio.wait_for(
    75	                process.communicate(), timeout=timeout
    76	            )
    77	            wall_clock = time.time() - start_time
    78	
    79	            output = stdout.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    80	            err_output = stderr.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    81	
    82	            return BackendResult(
    83	                success=process.returncode == 0,
    84	                output=output,
    85	                wall_clock_seconds=wall_clock,
    86	                token_usage=TokenUsage(),  # CLI doesn't report tokens directly
    87	                error=err_output if process.returncode != 0 else None,
    88	            )
    89	        except TimeoutError:
    90	            return BackendResult(
    91	                success=False,
    92	                wall_clock_seconds=time.time() - start_time,
    93	                error=f"Timeout after {timeout}s",
    94	            )
    95	        except FileNotFoundError:
    96	            return BackendResult(
    97	                success=False,
    98	                error=f"Command not found: {self._command}",
    99	            )
   100	
   101	    async def health_check(self) -> bool:
   102	        """Check if claude CLI is available."""
   103	        return shutil.which(self._command) is not None

   106	    def from_config(cls, config: AgentBackendConfig) -> ClaudeCodeBackend:
   107	        return cls(
   108	            command=config.command,
   109	            args=config.args,
   110	            env=config.env,
   111	            timeout_seconds=config.timeout_seconds,
   112	        )
   130	                # non-assistant message (e.g. the user echo) returns None → skip.
   131	                if message_texts:
   132	                    texts = message_texts
   133	
   134	            usage = event.get("usage")
   135	            if isinstance(usage, dict):
   136	                input_tokens += _coerce_int(usage.get("input_tokens")) or _coerce_int(
   137	                    usage.get("prompt_tokens")
   138	                )
   139	                output_tokens += _coerce_int(
   140	                    usage.get("output_tokens")
   141	                ) or _coerce_int(usage.get("completion_tokens"))
   142	                total_tokens += _coerce_int(usage.get("total_tokens"))
   143	
   144	        if total_tokens == 0:
   145	            total_tokens = input_tokens + output_tokens
   146	
   147	        usage_obj = TokenUsage(
   148	            input_tokens=input_tokens,
   149	            output_tokens=output_tokens,
   150	            total_tokens=total_tokens,
   151	        )
   152	        return "".join(texts), usage_obj

   154	    async def execute_task(
   155	        self,
   156	        task_description: str,
   157	        affected_files: list[str],
   158	        working_dir: str,
   159	        ablation: AblationFlags,
   160	        timeout_seconds: int = 300,
   161	    ) -> BackendResult:
   162	        """Execute a task via the `pi` CLI and stream-parse the NDJSON output."""
   163	        timeout = timeout_seconds if timeout_seconds is not None else self._timeout
   164	        start_time = time.time()
   165	
   166	        files_context = "\n".join(f"- {f}" for f in affected_files)
   167	        prompt = f"{task_description}\n\nFiles to work on:\n{files_context}"
   168	
   169	        cmd = self._build_command(prompt)
   170	
   171	        try:
   172	            env = {**os.environ, **self._env}
   173	            process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(
   174	                *cmd,
   175	                stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
   176	                stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
   177	                cwd=working_dir,
   178	                env=env,
   179	            )
   180	            stdout, stderr = await asyncio.wait_for(
   181	                process.communicate(), timeout=timeout
   182	            )
   183	            wall_clock = time.time() - start_time
   184	
   185	            raw = stdout.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
   186	            err_output = stderr.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
   187	
   188	            if process.returncode != 0:
   189	                return BackendResult(
   190	                    success=False,
   191	                    output=raw,
   192	                    wall_clock_seconds=wall_clock,
   193	                    error=err_output or f"pi exited {process.returncode}",
   194	                )
   195	
   196	            output, usage = self._parse_ndjson(raw)
   197	            return BackendResult(
   198	                success=True,
   199	                output=output,
   200	                wall_clock_seconds=wall_clock,
   201	                token_usage=usage,
   202	            )
   203	        except TimeoutError:
   204	            return BackendResult(
   205	                success=False,
   206	                wall_clock_seconds=time.time() - start_time,
   207	                error=f"Timeout after {timeout}s",
   208	            )
   209	        except FileNotFoundError:
   210	            return BackendResult(
   211	                success=False,
   212	                error=f"Command not found: {self._command}",
   213	            )
   214	
   215	    async def health_check(self) -> bool:
   216	        """Check if the `pi` CLI is available."""

    88	class OcrRunError(RuntimeError):
    89	    """Raised when ``ocr review`` fails to produce a readable result."""
    90	
    91	
    92	def run_ocr(cwd: Path, *, timeout_seconds: int = 900) -> dict[str, Any]:
    93	    """Run ``ocr review`` over *cwd* and return its parsed JSON result.
    94	
    95	    Workspace mode by default (matches the diff every other vendor reviews
    96	    from the packet, since OCR runs in the same worktree before any round's
    97	    fix commit). ``REVIEW_BASE_REF``/``REVIEW_HEAD_REF`` env vars switch to
    98	    range mode when both are set.
    99	    """
   100	    # A directory, not mkstemp: mkstemp pre-creates the file itself, which
   101	    # would defeat the "ocr never wrote it" check below (the file would
   102	    # already exist, just empty, on every failure path).
   103	    tmp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="ocr-review-")
   104	    output_path = Path(tmp_dir) / "result.json"
   105	    try:
   106	        cmd = [
   107	            "ocr", "review", "--format", "json", "--audience", "agent",
   108	            "--output", str(output_path),
   109	        ]
   110	        from_ref = os.environ.get("REVIEW_BASE_REF")
   111	        to_ref = os.environ.get("REVIEW_HEAD_REF")
   112	        if from_ref and to_ref:
   113	            cmd.extend(["--from", from_ref, "--to", to_ref])
   114	        result = subprocess.run(
   115	            cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout_seconds,
   116	            cwd=str(cwd),
   117	        )
   118	        if result.returncode != 0 and not output_path.exists():
   119	            raise OcrRunError(
   120	                f"ocr review exited {result.returncode}: {result.stderr[:500]}"
   121	            )
   122	        text = output_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
   123	        if not text.strip():
   124	            raise OcrRunError("ocr review produced an empty output file")
   125	        return json.loads(text)
   126	    finally:
   127	        shutil.rmtree(tmp_dir, ignore_errors=True)
   128	
   129	
   130	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   131	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
   132	    parser.add_argument(
   133	        "--change-id", default=os.environ.get("OCR_CHANGE_ID", "unknown"),
   134	    )
   135	    parser.add_argument(
   136	        "--review-type", default=os.environ.get("OCR_REVIEW_TYPE", "implementation"),
   137	    )
   138	    parser.add_argument("--repo", default=".")
   139	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
   140	
   141	    # Consume and discard stdin (the review packet body): OCR reads the diff
   142	    # itself and does not need a pre-built packet.
   143	    if not sys.stdin.isatty():
   144	        try:
   145	            sys.stdin.read()
   540	    *,
   541	    cwd: Path,
   542	    timeout_seconds: int = 120,
   543	) -> Caller | None:
   544	    """Build a subprocess-based caller from a vendor's CLI config, or None.
   545	
   546	    Deliberately does not reuse ``CliVendorAdapter.dispatch``/``review``
   547	    mode: that mode hard-codes findings-schema output (e.g. grok's
   548	    ``--json-schema``), the wrong shape for a fact-check verdict. Every
   549	    vendor in agents.yaml already declares an ``alternative`` dispatch mode
   550	    with the flags its own CLI needs for a plain, non-schema-constrained
   551	    prompt (``--print`` for claude, ``exec -s workspace-write`` for codex,
   552	    ``--prompt-file /dev/stdin`` for grok, and so on) — using a single
   553	    hard-coded Claude flag set (``--print --allowedTools``) here made the
   554	    pass silently no-op for every other vendor, since those flags mean
   555	    nothing to their CLIs. This reads that per-vendor mode instead. Returns
   556	    ``None`` (never raises) when the binary is not on PATH, or when the
   557	    vendor declares no synchronous ``alternative``/``quick`` mode to build
   558	    the command from — callers pass that straight to :func:`run` as
   559	    ``caller=None``, which skips gracefully rather than guessing flags.
   560	
   561	    Read-only-ness is a property of the fact-check prompt (it only ever
   562	    asks for a verdict, never invites an edit), not of the CLI's own
   563	    tool-permission flags — the same design already used for grok/agy/pi's
   564	    review-mode dispatch (see agents.yaml's comments on those vendors).
   565	    """
   566	    import shutil
   567	    import subprocess
   568	
   569	    command = getattr(cli_config, "command", None)
   570	    if not command or shutil.which(command) is None:
   571	        return None
   572	    dispatch_modes = getattr(cli_config, "dispatch_modes", None) or {}
   573	    mode_config = dispatch_modes.get("alternative") or dispatch_modes.get("quick")
   574	    if mode_config is None or getattr(mode_config, "async_dispatch", False):
   575	        return None
   576	    mode_args = list(getattr(mode_config, "args", None) or [])
   577	    model = resolve_economy_model(vendor)
   578	    model_flag = getattr(cli_config, "model_flag", None)
   579	    prompt_via_stdin = getattr(cli_config, "prompt_via_stdin", True)
   580	
   581	    def _caller(system_prompt: str, user_prompt: str) -> str:
   582	        full_prompt = system_prompt + "\n\n" + user_prompt
   583	        cmd = [command, *mode_args]
   584	        if model and model_flag:
   585	            cmd.extend([model_flag, model])
   586	        stdin_text = full_prompt if prompt_via_stdin else None
   587	        if not prompt_via_stdin:
   588	            cmd.append(full_prompt)
   589	        result = subprocess.run(
   590	            cmd,
   591	            input=stdin_text,
   592	            capture_output=True,
   593	            text=True,
   594	            timeout=timeout_seconds,
   595	            cwd=str(cwd),
   596	        )
   597	        if result.returncode != 0 and not result.stdout.strip():
   598	            raise RuntimeError(
   599	                f"fact-check caller exited {result.returncode}: {result.stderr[:300]}"
   600	            )
   601	        return result.stdout
   602	
   603	    return _caller

   112	
   113	## Output
   114	
   115	- Vendor stdout displayed inline.
   116	- Default mode: no files created, no commits, no worktree changes.
   117	- `--write` mode: changes occur only inside `quick-<slug>` worktree and branch.
   118	- No OpenSpec artifacts created unless the prompt explicitly asks for planning,
   119	  in which case use `/plan-feature` instead.
   120	
   121	## Semantic Code Context
   122	
   123	`quick-task` bypasses OpenSpec, so it has no `change_id`/`package_id` and therefore **no
   124	declared work-package read scope** — and no scope is invented for it. Every request it
   125	makes today returns `out_of_scope` / `no_declared_scope` and no section at all. Widening to
   126	the repository root to make injection "work everywhere" is exactly the failure the
   127	capability exists to prevent, so this skill receives nothing until it declares a scope.
   128	
   129	The section is optional in any case: `SEMANTIC_CONTEXT_INJECTION` defaults **off** and
   130	ri-13 owns enablement. The protocol is owned once by `context-engineering/SKILL.md`; this

   108	def _pick_fix_mode(adapter: Any) -> str | None:
   109	    """Prefer a write-capable dispatch mode over read-only review."""
   110	    can_dispatch = getattr(adapter, "can_dispatch", None)
   111	    if not callable(can_dispatch):
   112	        return None
   113	    for mode in ("alternative", "quick", "review"):
   114	        try:
   115	            if can_dispatch(mode):
   116	                return mode
   117	        except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — adapter availability is best-effort
   118	            continue
   119	    return None

     1	---
     2	name: quick-task
     3	description: Delegate small ad-hoc tasks to any configured vendor without OpenSpec ceremony
     4	category: Development
     5	tags: [vendor, dispatch, quick, micro-task]
     6	triggers:
     7	  - "quick task"
     8	  - "rescue"
     9	  - "quick fix"
    10	requires:
    11	  coordinator:
    12	    required: []
    13	    safety: []
    14	    enriching: []
    15	---
    16	
    17	# Quick Task
    18	
    19	Delegate a small ad-hoc task (bug investigation, code explanation, small
    20	read-only review, or explicitly isolated quick fix) directly to any configured
    21	vendor. Bypasses OpenSpec planning, but does not bypass the local CLI mutation
    22	boundary.
    23	
    24	Inspired by the `/codex:rescue` command from [codex-plugin-cc](https://github.com/openai/codex-plugin-cc).
    25	
    26	## Arguments
    27	
    28	`$ARGUMENTS` - The task prompt to send to the vendor
    29	
    30	Optional flags:
    31	- `--vendor <name>` — Dispatch to a specific vendor (e.g., `codex`, `claude`, `gemini`). Default: first available.
    32	- `--timeout <seconds>` — Override default timeout (default: 300s / 5 minutes)
    33	- `--write <slug>` — Allow file writes by first creating/entering a managed
    34	  worktree named `quick-<slug>`. Without this flag, quick-task is read-only by
    35	  default.
    36	
    37	## Prerequisites
    38	
    39	- At least one vendor CLI installed and configured in `agents.yaml`
    40	- Vendor must have a `quick` dispatch mode defined
    41	
    42	## Steps
    43	
    44	### 1. Parse Arguments
    45	
    46	Extract the task prompt, optional `--vendor`, `--timeout`, and `--write <slug>`
    47	flags from arguments.
    48	
    49	### 1.5. Enforce Read-Only or Isolated Write Mode
    50	
    51	Quick-task is read-only by default in local CLI execution. In default mode, add
    52	this instruction to the vendor prompt:
    53	
    54	```
    55	This quick task is read-only. Do not create, modify, delete, format, commit, or
    56	push files. Return findings and suggested patches in text only.
    57	```
    58	
    59	If `--write <slug>` is supplied, enter a managed worktree before dispatch:
    60	
    61	```bash
    62	CHANGE_ID="quick-<slug>"
    63	eval "$(python3 "<skill-base-dir>/../worktree/scripts/worktree.py" setup "$CHANGE_ID")"
    64	cd "$WORKTREE_PATH"
    65	python3 "<skill-base-dir>/../shared/checkout_policy.py" require-mutation
    66	```
    67	
    68	Write-mode quick tasks must push their branch and use PR review before any work
    69	reaches main.
    70	
    71	### 2. Complexity Check
    72	
    73	If the prompt exceeds 500 words OR references more than 5 file paths, emit a warning:
    74	
    75	```

name: validate-packages
description: "Validation scripts for work packages, parallel zones, and work results"

tags: [validation, packages, parallel, infrastructure]

# Validate Packages Infrastructure Skill

Non-user-invocable infrastructure skill that bundles validation scripts for the parallel workflow.

## Scripts

### `<skill-base-dir>/scripts/validate_work_packages.py`

Validates `work-packages.yaml` against the JSON schema.

**Usage**:
```bash
python3 "<skill-base-dir>/scripts/validate_work_packages.py" <path-to-work-packages.yaml>
```

**Checks**: schema compliance, depends_on references, DAG cycles, lock key canonicalization
**Exit codes**: 0 = VALID, 1 = INVALID (details on stderr)

This script is deliberately git-free — it validates a file in isolation and is
run against fixtures with no repository. Context-impact checking needs a diff,
so it lives in a sibling script rather than here.

### `<skill-base-dir>/scripts/validate_context_impact.py`

Fails a work package that invalidates derived project context it never declared.

**Usage**:
```bash
python3 "<skill-base-dir>/scripts/validate_context_impact.py" <path-to-work-packages.yaml> --base main
python3 "<skill-base-dir>/scripts/validate_context_impact.py" <path> --changed-file docs/guide.md --json
```

**Exit codes**: 0 = VALID, 1 = INVALID, 2 = usage or rule-table error

`--base` resolves changed files with `git diff --name-only <base>...HEAD`, so it
sees **committed** changes only — which is what a pre-merge gate should judge.
While iterating, pass `--changed-file` explicitly (repeatable) to classify
working-tree paths; that path also takes no git dependency at all, which is how
ri-09 will feed it a checkpoint's own file list.

#### Context surfaces

A package declares which surfaces it may invalidate in an optional
`context_impact.surfaces` list. Each surface names the producer that owns
refreshing it, so a declaration is directly actionable:

| Surface | Owning producer / skill |
|---|---|
| `capabilities` | `openspec.projection` |
| `apis` | `api.contracts` |
| `architecture` | `refresh-architecture` |
| `decisions` | `decisions.timeline` |
| `documentation` | `documentation.inventory` |
| `semantic_code` | `code-search` index |

#### Enforcement

The declaration is a *reviewable hint*, never evidence of completeness — a
planner can omit it. The authoritative signal is the package's changed files
(intersected with `scope.write_allow`, minus `scope.deny`) plus the change's
`contracts.openapi.files`, classified by the glob rule table at
`openspec/schemas/context-impact-rules.yaml`.

Enforcement keys off whether the block exists, so the gate can be strict without
a flag day:

| Package state | Implied surface not declared | Result |
|---|---|---|
| has `context_impact` | no rationale | `undeclared` → **exit 1** |
| has `context_impact` | rationale with `approved_by` | `rationalized` → pass |
| has `context_impact` | nothing implied | `declared` → pass |
| no `context_impact` | anything implied | `unmigrated` → pass, reports inferred surfaces |

Declaring is opt-in but one-way: once the block is present it must be complete.
An empty `surfaces: []` is a real "affects nothing" assertion, checked strictly —
not a placeholder. A rationale needs both a non-empty `reason` and a non-empty
`approved_by`, and a rationale for a surface the detector does *not* imply fails
as `spurious_rationale`, so rationales cannot be pre-sprinkled.

`--strict-legacy` promotes `unmigrated` to a failure, so the repository can flip
to full enforcement in one flag once packages are migrated.

#### Rule table

`context-impact-rules.yaml` maps globs to surfaces and is deliberately data, not
code — reviewability is the point of this gate. Every surface must have at least
one rule; a surface with no rule silently stops being detectable, which the test
suite pins. Loading fails on a missing file rather than yielding an empty rule
set.

#### Downstream scope resolution

`context_impact.index_scopes(package)` resolves a package's `scope.read_allow`
and `scope.deny` (deny wins) for semantic indexing and scoped context injection.
It resolves rather than duplicates — adding a parallel copy of the globs under
`context_impact` would create two sources of truth.

### `<skill-base-dir>/scripts/parallel_zones.py`

Validates scope non-overlap for parallel work packages.

**Usage**:
```bash
python3 "<skill-base-dir>/scripts/parallel_zones.py" --validate-packages <path> [--json]
```

**Exit codes**: 0 = no overlap, 1 = overlap detected

### `<skill-base-dir>/scripts/validate_work_result.py`

Validates work results against the work-queue-result schema.

**Usage**:
```bash
python3 "<skill-base-dir>/scripts/validate_work_result.py" <path-to-result.json>
```

**Exit codes**: 0 = valid, 1 = invalid

### `<skill-base-dir>/scripts/validate_schema.py`

Generic JSON schema validator. When the document it is pointed at is an
architecture artifact, make that artifact current first — validating a stale
graph reports the shape of an analysis nobody is going to act on:

```bash
# Ensure architecture artifacts are current, immediately before the first read.
# `--ensure` is `--check` plus a staged refresh only when the check is not fresh,
# so on an already-fresh checkout it writes nothing. PYTHON must name the same
# interpreter this repository's architecture targets use: the check runs in-process
# and the pipeline runs in a subprocess, and if the two disagree about which
# optional grammars are importable they report permanent, unfixable drift.
ARCH_PY="${PYTHON:-python3}"
if "$ARCH_PY" "<skill-base-dir>/../refresh-architecture/scripts/run_architecture.py" --ensure --python "$ARCH_PY"; then
  ARCH_FRESHNESS="ensured"
else
  ARCH_FRESHNESS="DEGRADED"
  echo "DEGRADED: architecture artifacts could not be made current; the last known-good analysis is left intact but unverified. Report every architecture-derived finding below as unverified rather than as current." >&2
fi
```

The ensure call belongs here, in the caller's step, and not inside
`validate_schema.py`: the script takes an explicit document path, is run against
fixtures with no repository, and must keep validating the file it was handed.

**Usage**:
```bash
python3 "<skill-base-dir>/scripts/validate_schema.py" <schema-path> <document-path>
```

### `<skill-base-dir>/scripts/architecture_schema.json`

JSON schema for architecture analysis artifacts.

     1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
     2	"""Parallel modification zone analyzer.
     3	
     4	Identifies independent subgraphs in the canonical architecture graph to
     5	determine which modules can be safely modified in parallel.
     6	
     7	Uses only stdlib dependencies -- graph algorithms are implemented via
     8	union-find (connected components) and BFS (transitive dependents).
     9	"""
    10	
    11	from __future__ import annotations
    12	
    13	import argparse
    14	import json
    15	import logging
    16	import sys
    17	from collections import defaultdict
    18	from pathlib import Path
    19	
    20	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    21	
    22	_SCRIPT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
    23	sys.path.insert(0, str(_SCRIPT_DIR))
    24	# Sibling skill for validate_work_packages imports
    25	_VALIDATE_PACKAGES_DIR = _SCRIPT_DIR.parent.parent / "validate-packages" / "scripts"
    26	if str(_VALIDATE_PACKAGES_DIR) not in sys.path:
    27	    sys.path.insert(0, str(_VALIDATE_PACKAGES_DIR))
    28	from arch_utils.constants import DEPENDENCY_EDGE_TYPES  # noqa: E402
    29	from arch_utils.graph_io import load_graph  # noqa: E402
    30	from arch_utils.determinism import generated_at_iso  # noqa: E402
    31	from arch_utils.traversal import reachable_from  # noqa: E402
    32	
    33	
    34	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    35	# Union-Find for weakly connected components
    36	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    37	
    38	class UnionFind:
    39	    """Disjoint-set / union-find with path compression and union by rank."""
    40	
    41	    def __init__(self, elements: list[str]) -> None:
    42	        self._parent: dict[str, str] = {e: e for e in elements}
    43	        self._rank: dict[str, int] = {e: 0 for e in elements}
    44	
    45	    def find(self, x: str) -> str:
    46	        root = x
    47	        while self._parent[root] != root:
    48	            root = self._parent[root]
    49	        # Path compression
    50	        while self._parent[x] != root:
    51	            self._parent[x], x = root, self._parent[x]
    52	        return root
    53	
    54	    def union(self, a: str, b: str) -> None:
    55	        ra, rb = self.find(a), self.find(b)
    56	        if ra == rb:
    57	            return
    58	        # Union by rank
    59	        if self._rank[ra] < self._rank[rb]:
    60	            ra, rb = rb, ra
    61	        self._parent[rb] = ra
    62	        if self._rank[ra] == self._rank[rb]:
    63	            self._rank[ra] += 1
    64	
    65	    def components(self) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    66	        """Return mapping of root -> list of members."""
    67	        groups: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
    68	        for element in self._parent:
    69	            groups[self.find(element)].append(element)
    70	        return dict(groups)
    71	
    72	
    73	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    74	# Dependency-edge filtering
    75	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    76	
    77	def _is_dependency_edge(edge: dict) -> bool:
    78	    """Return True if this edge should be considered a dependency link."""
    79	    return edge.get("type") in DEPENDENCY_EDGE_TYPES
    80

   129	# Upper bound on time spent queued behind the concurrency cap. Queueing is
